title: David Crowley upsets democratic socialist Francesca Hong in Wisconsin governor primary
summary: NBC News projects that Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive backed by Gov. Tony Evers, narrowly defeated Hong, a democratic socialist state lawmaker, in the key battleground state.
story: Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley has won the Democratic primary in Wisconsin’s race for governor, NBC News projects, dealing a major upset to democratic socialist Francesca Hong.

The result marks a dramatic turnaround for Crowley, who had dropped out of the race roughly a month ago after initially struggling to gain traction only to re-enter days later with outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers’ endorsement.

Hong, a state lawmaker from Madison, had led in the polls in the final stretch of the race, but faced growing scrutiny over her past controversial positions and general election viability. Her loss is a setback for progressives, who have found success in other high-profile primaries around the country this year against establishment-backed candidates.

Crowley will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany, who is backed by President Donald Trump, in a general election that will be one of the marquee gubernatorial matchups this fall. Crowley took 39.8% of the Democratic primary vote to 39.4% for Hong with 98% of the expected vote tallied.

Crowley, 40, has served as Milwaukee County executive since 2020. Before that, he was a member of the state Assembly representing an urban Milwaukee district. As recently as late July, he was in the single digits in the well-regarded Marquette University Law School poll, with a large plurality of voters behind Hong, but more than a third saying they were still undecided.
His victory marks the final unexpected development of a volatile primary that had long lacked a clear front-runner.

Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez, who some Democrats expected would emerge as a leading centrist contender, abruptly dropped out of the race in mid-July amid campaign finance reporting issues. A few weeks later, former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes, a progressive who was the party’s 2022 Senate nominee, ended his bid.
In between those moves, Crowley relaunched his campaign after initially struggling to gain traction in a crowded field, part of a last-ditch push by moderate Democrats to find an alternative to Hong.
Evers, a popular governor who chose not to run for a third term, went to bat for Crowley on the campaign trail, arguing that he was the most electable candidate in the primary.

The message seemed to land with some voters. Ali Plummer of Madison told NBC News that she “voted for Crowley because I am a risk-averse person, and I really was reading a lot about who has the chances to beat Tom Tiffany in the larger election.”
But Plummer was part of a “split-vote couple” with Shawn Bass, who voted for Hong.
“I really think that she has a great platform for talking about universal healthcare, talking about universal childcare,” Bass said.

Crowley’s campaign and allied outside groups also spent $4 million on ads during the primary, according to AdImpact — well more than any of his Democratic rivals. By comparison, the Hong campaign and groups supporting her spent less than a half-million dollars on ads.

Crowley faced some of his own controversies. Shortly after he re-entered the race, NBC News reported on a years-old social media account registered to him featuring incendiary posts about women and race, along with derogatory LGBTQ references.
But the focus in the closing weeks of the primary was on Hong, who faced concerns over her ability to win in November in one of the most closely divided states in the country.

She walked back her past calls to defund and abolish the police, eliminate the U.S. Senate and cancel Thanksgiving. And while she has been fiercely critical of Israel and its leaders over the war in Gaza, she did not make the issue a central part of her campaign message, as other progressives have.

Still, Hong did not shy away from the democratic socialist label and held a rally with left-wing streamer Hasan Piker and Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., one of the more liberal members of the House. Notably, Hong did not receive endorsements from the country’s leading democratic socialist voices, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez., who have waded into other contentious Democratic primary fights.

Hong also faced very few attacks from her Democratic rivals. In the only debate of the primary late last month, none of her opponents directly criticized her. On the airwaves, a pro-Crowley outside group only started running a TV ad targeting Hong in the closing days of the race, saying her “record is a distraction we can’t afford.”

Meanwhile, a group tied to the Republican Governors Association has spent nearly $3 million on ads casting her as too liberal — an apparent effort to boost the party’s preferred general election opponent in the primary.

Candidates aside from Hong and Crowley played a significant role on Tuesday, pulling a combined 20% of the vote. They included Rodriguez and Barnes, who were each taking nearly 4% support. A Wisconsin judge had ruled that voters who returned absentee ballots could not request new ones, even if the candidates they backed were no longer in the race.
Progressive state Sen. Kelda Roys was in third place, just shy of 8%.
On the GOP side, Tiffany — who has represented the 7th Congressional District, which comprises much of the northern part of the state, since 2020 — easily won the party’s gubernatorial nomination.
In a speech to supporters, Tiffany said, “Stand with me as we protect the Wisconsin way of life, and stand with me as we move Wisconsin forward.”
Democrats have held Wisconsin’s governorship since 2019, and are hoping to flip control of at least one state legislative chamber for the first time since the 2010 election.

The winner of the Crowley-Tiffany matchup will hold power during the 2028 presidential election. Tiffany voted against certifying Joe Biden’s 2020 victories in Arizona and Pennsylvania as a member of the House.
If Crowley wins in November, he would the first Black governor in Wisconsin history.

title: Kansas father kills 4 children and wife before turning gun on himself, authorities say
summary: The children were identified as girls ages 9, 5 and 3 and a boy, 7.  An official said the father had been reported for “aggressive behavior” in the past.
story: A Kansas man who police said was previously contacted for “aggressive behavior” fatally shot his four young children and their mother before he turned the gun on himself Tuesday, authorities said.

Officers were already at an unrelated car crash two blocks away when they were summoned to a single-family home in Windfield based on a 911 call from a man who identified himself as the shooter, Windfield Police Chief Robbie DeLong said.

“At approximately 8:50 a.m., our officers received a 911 call from a male individual who stated that he had killed his entire family and he was getting ready to kill himself,” DeLong said at a news conference.

The first officer to arrive approached the residence but retreated after hearing a single gunshot, DeLong said. Authorities set up around the home under the assumption they had an armed, barricaded person on their hands, he said.
A little more than two hours after the 911 call, with a regional SWAT team and Cowley County sheriff’s deputies joining the standoff, authorities breached the home and found the bodies, DeLong said.
“I want to make something very clear to the community,” he said. “This was an isolated incident. There is no ongoing threat.”
The dead were identified as the suspect, Ronald H. Williams, 53; mother Kelly L. George, 44; Carol A. Williams, 9; Ronald H. Williams Jr., 7; Sarah K. Williams, 5; and Kelly M. McGee Williams, 3.

DeLong said that police had contact with the father as recently as the last few weeks and that officers have responded to the area of the family’s home in the past based on reports of gunfire but were unsuccessful finding evidence.
“We have calls of just aggressive behavior, but not enough really to act on,” he said.

Williams was a registered sex offender, according to the state sex offender registry. In 1998, a judge accepted guilty pleas by Williams to two felony counts of attempted indecent liberties with a child and one count of battery involving the same victim, a 15-year-old girl, according to Kansas criminal court records.
The Kansas Bureau of Investigation (KBI) has joined the probe into Tuesday’s violence, with a key goal of identifying a motive, DeLong said.
KBI Special Agent in Charge Jason Diaz said agents would seek to interview relatives as well as neighbors.
If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 or go to 988lifeline.org to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Minnesota GOP picks Lisa Demuth over Trump-backed Mike Lindell for governor against Democrat Amy Klobuchar
summary: Demuth, the state House speaker, defeated Trump-endorsed Lindell for the Republican nomination, NBC News projects, while Klobuchar romped in her primary.
story: Minnesota state House Speaker Lisa Demuth won the Republican primary for governor, NBC News projects, defeating Trump ally Mike Lindell and setting up a general election matchup against Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar.

Demuth’s victory was an upset over Lindell, the MyPillow founder and election conspiracy theorist. Lindell had been leading in limited public polling heading into Election Day, and President Donald Trump endorsed him.

But attacks on Lindell from fellow Republicans — including questions about his residency raised by the chairman of the Minnesota Republican Party — hampered his campaign in the final weeks before the primary, as members of the Minnesota GOP sought a nominee who could beat Klobuchar in the general election.
Lindell has faced several legal challenges since 2020, when he championed Trump’s debunked theories about the 2020 presidential election, which former President Joe Biden won.
At a Minnesota Farmfest forum this month, Klobuchar appeared alongside three GOP candidates for governor and accused each of them of being “a rubber stamp of Donald Trump.”

Demuth and other Republicans — including Trump — have attacked Democrats in the blue state over two sprawling fraud scandals involving Medicaid and pandemic aid. Among the allegations were that hundreds of millions of dollars that had been earmarked for welfare programs were stolen.

At the farm event, Demuth blamed “incompetent Democrat control” for the fraud cases, and she has pointed on the campaign trail to the Fraud Prevention Agency Oversight Committee, which she established leading the state House.

In January, Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, who had planned to run for a third term, decided to drop his re-election campaign, citing the attacks over the fraud cases. A few weeks later, Klobuchar launched her campaign. She is one of four senators to run for governor this year.

Still, Republicans will have to overcome political trends in Minnesota in November to win the Governor’s Residence. Then-Vice President Kamala Harris won the state by about 4 percentage points in the most recent presidential election, when Walz was her running mate.

title: Progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan wins Minnesota Democratic Senate primary
summary: Flanagan defeated Rep. Angie Craig, NBC News projects, in yet another nominating contest that exposed Democratic ideological divides.
story: Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan has won the Democratic primary for the Senate in Minnesota, NBC News projects, notching another major victory for her party’s progressive wing.

Flanagan defeated moderate Rep. Angie Craig in the race to succeed retiring Sen. Tina Smith, who endorsed Flanagan along with Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and other progressive leaders. She would be the first Native American woman in the Senate if she is elected in November.

“This entire campaign has been about the many versus the money,” Flanagan told NBC News’ “Meet the Press Now” on the eve of the primary. Craig and her allies combined to spend nearly $20 million on the airwaves, while Flanagan and her allies spent $4.7 million, according to AdImpact.

“I’m running to make sure that people can afford the lives they want to live,” Flanagan said. “I want to get big money out of our politics, and I want to fight for things like ‘Medicare for All’ so that people aren’t just paying for health insurance but actually have access to health care.”

Flanagan criticized Craig, who is in her fourth term, for not standing up enough to President Donald Trump’s administration, which Craig disputed. Craig, who held a competitive House seat in the Twin Cities metro area, had argued that she was the best candidate to win in November.

Immigration became a major dividing line in the race after federal agents shot and killed two U.S. citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in Minneapolis this year amid the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement surge.

Craig faced criticism for having voted for the Laken Riley Act, an immigration detention measure that Trump signed into law shortly after he started his second term in January 2025. Craig said she later regretted that vote. Flanagan has called for abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, saying in a recent Minnesota Public Radio debate that ICE “has to be ripped apart.” Flanagan said she does support immigration enforcement to ensure secure borders.

Flanagan, meanwhile, faced criticism from Craig over Minnesota’s handling of fraud in social services programs, with Craig suggesting that Republicans would be eager to use the issue against Flanagan in the fall. Flanagan accused Craig of parroting “Republican talking points.”

Asked during their debate whether she had a role in responding to the fraud scandal, Flanagan said, “The governor has taken the lead here, and the administration has been aggressive internally in working to stop fraud, prevent it from happening in the first place.”
Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, who decided not to run for re-election, stayed neutral in the Senate primary. But his wife, Gwen, backed Craig over Flanagan, the governor’s ticketmate.
After a divisive primary, Flanagan’s next task will be to unite the party as Democrats turn to November. She told “Meet the Press Now” that Democrats would come together to take on Trump.

“Congresswoman Craig and I will be unified in making sure that Democrats hold this seat no matter what happens. We can’t afford to give this Donald Trump one more seat in the United States Senate,” she said.
Craig said during the debate that she would support Flanagan if she won the primary.

“We have an existential crisis in our nation with Trump and Republicans, and so I would be right by the lieutenant governor’s side asking my supporters to support her,” Craig said. “The most important thing in this election is that we beat Republicans. That’s what matters.”

On the Republican side, former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya won the Senate primary, NBC News projects. Although Trump did not endorse in the primary, Tafoya had support from National Republican Senatorial Campaign Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., as national Republicans viewed her as the only contender who could put the race in play.

Tafoya, a self-described “pro-choice” Republican, has faced some questions about her conservative credentials. She did not win the state GOP’s endorsement at the May convention, where delegates instead backed retired Navy SEAL Adam Schwarze.
She pitched herself as a political outsider, pledging in a campaign ad to “crack down on corruption, stop illegal immigrants from voting in our elections and to keep men out of women’s sports.”
Republicans are optimistic the race could be competitive in the fall, as they have made some gains in the state in the Trump era.

Trump lost Minnesota by 4 percentage points in 2024, winning 47% of the vote, which was the best performance by a GOP presidential candidate in two decades. But it has also been 20 years since Republicans last won a statewide election in Minnesota, when Tim Pawlenty was re-elected as governor in 2006.

title: Trump says security threat spurred secret plane swap in Turkey
summary: The president spoke for the first time about a previously undisclosed flight after the NATO summit in July.
story: President Donald Trump confirmed Tuesday night that he secretly switched planes when he traveled back from Turkey in July, saying a security threat prompted the clandestine maneuver.
Trump told reporters that the “Secret Service and the military” made the decision.
“They wanted me to go on a different flight, a different plane,” he said. “I guess there was a threat out there.”

NBC News previously confirmed The Washington Post’s reporting that Trump surreptitiously moved to an unmarked jet using a catering truck on July 8 after having boarded Air Force One in front of cameras. He flew on the jet from Ankara to a base in the United Kingdom, while reporters and White House staff members believed he was on board Air Force One.
“I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk. I think it was at greater risk because that would be the plane I think that they would be more likely to go for,” Trump said Tuesday.
He did not elaborate on why the unmarked C-32 jet he boarded, whose call sign was not marked as Air Force One, made it a likelier target.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

NBC News also reported that the plane switch came, according to a U.S. official, amid a fresh Iranian plot to kill Trump, possibly involving a shoulder-fired missile aimed at Air Force One as it departed Turkey. Those left behind on the decoy plane included members of the media and senior White House staff members, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who are in the presidential line of succession.
Trump said he “didn’t really ask so much” about the threat, but he said he was “not surprised” there had been one.
“Any consequential president has a lot of threats. Nonconsequential presidents don’t get threatened, and I think that I may be the most consequential president,” he said.
Congressional Democrats are demanding a briefing from officials on the specifics of Trump’s flight last month and any security threats that surrounded it.

title: Democrat backed by Bernie Sanders wins primary as parties prepare to battle for the House
summary: Democrat Rebecca Cooke will face GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden again in Wisconsin, NBC News projects, as both parties nominated candidates in battleground districts.
story: Tuesday’s primaries are setting the matchups in around a half-dozen competitive House races that will be key to the fight for the House majority in November, including in a hotly contested Democratic target in Wisconsin.
Rebecca Cooke won the Democratic primary in Wisconsin’s 3rd District, NBC News projects, and will take on two-term GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden in the fall.
The race will be a rematch from 2024, when Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points even though Donald Trump carried the district by 7 points.

Cooke, a small-business owner, has touted her roots growing up on a dairy farm and tried to eschew political labels, boasting a range of supporters from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee to moderate groups like New Dems and Blue Dogs to a progressive icon in Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

“I am a Blue Dog and a New Dem, but I’m also very progressive where it counts,” Cooke told NBC News last year. “I don’t like the labels and the boxes that kind of have been created, because immediately, you know, you’re written off and ‘othered’ in your party because you’re this or because you’re that. And really, I’m just — I’m running because I’m for western Wisconsin, period.”

Republicans are looking to paint her as too far left for the district. Van Orden campaign spokesperson Grace Kim recently said in a statement that Cooke “has aligned herself with the most extreme elements of her party,” pointing to video of her saying she would support Zohran Mamdani for mayor of New York and calling for a ban on AR-15 rifles.

Cooke has proven to be a strong fundraiser, pulling in nearly $8.6 million to Van Orden’s $7.5 million this election cycle. And the race is sure to attract millions more: Super PACs from both parties have already reserved $9 million in airtime for the fall, according to AdImpact.

Democrats also hope they can put another Wisconsin race in play in November: the 1st District in the southeastern corner of the state, where GOP Rep. Bryan Steil is running for a fifth term with Trump’s endorsement. Trump won the district by less than 5 points in 2024.

Mitchell Berman, a former nurse at the Department of Veterans Affairs, won the Democratic primary, NBC News projects, after having decided to run for office after the Department of Government Efficiency’s efforts to slash the federal workforce.

“I got an email asking me to justify my job,” Berman told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. “Give Elon Musk three things that I did in the previous week as an ER nurse at the bedside at the VA. I realized, this is no longer about improving care for veterans.”
Berman’s fundraising has lagged behind that of Steil, who has raised $5.5 million this election cycle, while Berman has pulled in $713,000.

Democrats are also looking at Minnesota’s 1st District as a potential pickup, although it is further down the party’s list of targets, given Trump won the district in southern Minnesota by 12 points in 2024.
Trump has endorsed GOP Rep. Brad Finstad. High school teacher Jake Johnson won the Democratic primary, NBC News projects, and will face Finstad in November.
Republicans are looking to pick up Alabama’s 2nd District, in the southeastern corner of the state, after a redistricting effort redrew the state’s congressional lines.

The seat, represented by Democrat Shomari Figures, had been one of the state’s largely Black districts, but it shifted toward Republicans after the Supreme Court ruled in June that Alabama could use a different map preferred by state Republicans. In 2024, then-Vice President Kamala Harris won the old version of the district by 8 points, but Trump would have won it by about 14 points under the new lines.

Republicans have nominated state Rep. Rhett Marques, who will take on Figures in the fall. Marques is backed by prominent Republicans including Trump, top members of House GOP leadership and Sen. Katie Britt.
Republicans are also looking to make Minnesota’s open 2nd District competitive as they defend their narrow House majority.

Trump lost the district in the Twin Cities suburbs by 6 points in 2024, but it has been competitive in recent election cycles. And Democrats no longer have the benefit of incumbency, since Rep. Angie Craig vacated the seat to run for the Senate.
State Sen. Matt Little won the Democratic primary and will face GOP state Sen. Eric Pratt in the fall.

title: Democratic Rep. John Larson loses his primary to opponent calling for generational change
summary: The 14-term Connecticut Democrat lost to former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin in a heavily blue district, NBC News projects.
story: Democratic Rep. John Larson of Connecticut has lost his primary race to former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin, NBC News projects, becoming the latest example of Democratic voters’ push to sweep out incumbent House members and replace them with younger leadership.
See live results here

Larson, 78, has been a fixture in Connecticut politics, having served for more than a decade in the state Legislature and almost three decades in Congress. A former member of party leadership, he touted his work on Social Security in Congress and had been backed by the state’s congressional delegation, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and key unions.

But Bronin, 47, mounted a serious campaign against him, calling for generational change and arguing that President Donald Trump’s second term called for new energy and new direction from Democratic lawmakers. Bronin raised more money than Larson and won over party activists at the state convention, winning the state party’s endorsement.
Larson is the 10th House member to lose a primary this year: seven Democrats and three Republicans.

“In this moment, when Donald Trump is president, the job of a member of Congress isn’t just in the subcommittee rooms, it’s what you are doing outside the walls of the Capitol to build a movement,” Bronin said in a late May interview.

“Over these next two years, it’s so important to have Democratic members of Congress using that platform not just to give red-faced speeches to an empty chamber for the C-SPAN cameras, but to ... carry our message, to win people back who lost faith in our party.”

Asked Monday on NBC News’ “Meet the Press Now” about the movement for generational change in the Democratic Party, Larson said that “I think the change that we need is to continue to go after Donald Trump” and touted his “record of doing that.”

“I have the endorsement of more elected officials, every sitting member in the congressional delegation, because they understand what I’ve been able to deliver,” he said. “They understand that they’re able to work with me, and they understand what I’ve been able to accomplish on their behalf. Luke Bronin has no record. I’m running on a record of accomplishment and achievement.”

Bronin replied that Larson has been in office “for about 50 years, and for the last 10 years or so, I just think he’s gotten stuck in a routine. And I understand, you know, it’s hard to find anybody who does the same thing for 30 years and doesn’t get a little bit stuck in the routine, but this is not a moment that we can keep doing the same thing.”

title: River tubers’ 4-hour tour turned into 3 days of survival in remote Michigan woods
summary: Two women and a boy were rescued and hospitalized for scrapes, cuts, dehydration and exhaustion, the state Department of Natural Resources said.
story: Two women and a child who were tubing on a river last week ended up lost in remote Michigan woods for three days before rescuers found them safe, authorities said Tuesday.
Michigan State Police identified the three as Jazzmin Hock, 28, of Muskegon; her cousin, Sarah Vida, 28, of Muskegon; and Vida’s 9-year-old son, Kayden Kovalcik.
They were released after they were treated at medical facilities for scrapes, cuts, dehydration and exhaustion over the weekend, State Police Lt. Pat Agema said by email Tuesday.

Authorities said the tubes they were using deflated when they struck a logjam on the Muskegon River in Western Michigan. The tubes were found on the second day of a three-day water, air and land search, state police said in a statement.
The father of one of the women who were reported missing Wednesday told authorities he found his daughter’s vehicle parked at the Maple Island Boat Launch in Grant with a broken window, they said.
Family members had been unable to contact the three, the man told authorities, according to state police.

The tubers were rescued Friday amid dense woods and thick ground cover by two state troopers and three Michigan Department of Natural Resources conservation officers. The rescue was captured by bodycam video.
The video shows that as the rescuers heard voices, one said: “Hey. Let’s stop. And yell. Make some noise.”
Another on the rescue team said, “They’re just beyond that tree.”
“Oh, my God, really?” another responded.
When they reached the missing tubers, the 9-year-old boy excitedly told them what happened.
“We got lost on the river,” he said. “We went to the river, and we were on the river for four hours.”
State Trooper Zach Murphy embraced Hock and gave her a shirt. The body camera video showed she had cuts the length of her legs.
Conservation Officer Anna Cullen asked one of the survivors when she last had water. “I don’t even know,” the woman responded.

Conservation Officer Cameron Wright said in a statement that the trio were in a bad location, which, according to state police, was less than a mile northeast of the Mill Iron Road river vessel launch area on the Muskegon River in Muskegon.

“We knew this specific location is the most remote area that the tubers could have been pulled to, and it would be a bad spot to get lost because it’s the furthest point from any roads or houses,” he said.
The team tracked the lost tubers using ground patterns, Wright said.

“We could see in the middle of the log jam a path in the grass — the tubers came down some logs and went through water, then onto the riverbank and into the trees,” he said. “We were able to see where they entered the woods and requested assistance once we located footprints in the mud.”
The team followed the prints, as well as paths indicated by tipped-over ferns, bent grass and other dislocated foliage, before it reached the trio, he said.
Murphy said in a video call that he couldn’t believe his eyes when he came upon the tubers.
“The thought that kept going through my head was I can’t believe that three people, allegedly in bathing suits, with no shoes on, were making the trek through that swamp,” he said.
He called the rescue a “fourth-quarter, fourth-down, Hail Mary victory.”

title: Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman advance to GOP Senate primary runoff in South Carolina
summary: Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, will face another Republican in an Aug. 25 runoff for the party’s nomination, NBC News projects.
story: Appointed Sen. Darline Graham was forced into a Republican Senate primary runoff by Rep. Ralph Norman on Tuesday, raising the prospect that GOP voters will again reject a candidate endorsed by President Donald Trump.

Graham, who was appointed by South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster to fill the remainder of her late brother Lindsey Graham’s term in July, is looking to also take his place on the November ballot for a full six years in the Senate. Trump encouraged her to run and then endorsed her in a primary that featured 10 GOP candidates, including Norman, Rep. Russell Fry  and former Gov. Mark Sanford.
The winner of the Aug. 25 runoff will face Democrat Annie Andrews, a doctor who won her party’s primary in June.

Graham, the first woman ever to represent South Carolina in the Senate, has never held elected office before, and her thin résumé appeared to cost her with some voters in the first round of the primary, calling into question the power of Trump’s imprimatur.

“I understand that she’s lost a brother and lost someone very special to her, and I sympathize with that, but at the same time, I don’t think that it’s necessary just to give it to her,” Republican voter Bob Howell told NBC News in Lexington, South Carolina.
Asked about Trump endorsing Graham, Howell said, “I like President Trump, but I don’t think that that’s necessarily what sways my vote.”
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

Earlier this year, Trump’s favored candidate for governor, Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette, got pushed into a runoff against state Attorney General Alan Wilson. Trump then issued a rare dual endorsement of both candidates in the Republican primary runoff, which Wilson won. That was one of several races across the country this year in which Trump’s preferred candidate failed to win the Republican nomination for a high office.
The winner of this Republican runoff will be heavily favored to prevail in November in a state where a Democrat has not won a Senate seat since Fritz Hollings’ re-election in 1998.

Darline Graham, 62, replaced her older brother in the Senate after Lindsey Graham died July 11, after emergency personnel responded to a “cardiac arrest” call at his Capitol Hill home. The elder Graham had been seeking a fifth term in November and had already won a competitive primary in June.
Trump wasted little time in throwing his weight behind the younger Graham, issuing his “complete and total endorsement” on Truth Social on July 17, less than a week after her brother’s death.

In her brief tenure in the Senate, Graham has been centrally involved in one issue: passage of a measure, earlier this month, that would impose new sanctions on Russia and Iran. Lindsey Graham had been the chief proponent of an earlier version of the legislation, which focused on applying pressure to Russia. At Trump’s request, Iran provisions were added before the Senate re-named the measure for Lindsey Graham and passed it, 86-11.

“I think I’ve accomplished a whole lot in three weeks,” Darline Graham said after she cast her vote Tuesday, pointing to the sanctions bill and her vote to confirm Attorney General Todd Blanche. “I’m not being handed the seat. I realize that I have to earn votes, so I’m working really hard to do that.”
Graham added that she expected the race to move to a runoff.

Norman, who finished a distant third in the state’s Republican gubernatorial primary earlier this year, consistently supports Trump’s agenda in Congress. But Lindsey Graham was one of the president’s closest allies — Trump eulogized the late senator during a service at Washington National Cathedral — and that loyalty was reciprocated in the endorsement of Darline Graham.
Now, with most of the state’s Republican voters having cast ballots for her rivals, Graham will need to consolidate support quickly in order to keep a seat that has been in her family since 2003.

title: Why is the U.S. banning a ton of robot vacuums? Here’s what you should know
summary: The FCC banned foreign-made advanced robots, and robot vacuums fall under the new rules. Here’s what it means for the device you already own — and which models you can still buy.
story: Robots are having a moment with the federal government — and it’s not all positive. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently announced a ban on foreign-made advanced mobile robots, a category that covers a ton of different types of robots. And while you probably don’t have a walking, talking robot in your living room yet, you might have something else the ban touches: a robot vacuum.
That everyday cleaning gadget falls squarely into the category now facing new restrictions, and it has nothing to do with battery recalls or overheating parts. Here’s what you need to know.
Why are robot vacuums being banned?

Late last week, the FCC added advanced robotic devices and foreign-made power inverters to its Covered List, the government’s running roster of tech that’s considered too risky to trust. The list flags communications equipment and services the FCC says pose “an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons.”

What that means in practice is that anything on the list can’t get FCC equipment authorization. And without that authorization, a product typically can’t be imported, marketed or sold in the United States.

So why robots? According to the FCC’s National Security Determination, it comes down to what these devices can see and record. Robots are often packed with high-tech sensors that are constantly gathering data about the spaces they move through.

The concern isn’t just what the sensors collect, though. It’s also how the devices connect. Because robots typically operate on networks, the FCC notes they’re vulnerable to the same risks as any connected device: getting hacked, having data stolen or even losing control of the device itself.
What is covered under the robot ban?
While the ban seems mostly aimed at humanoid and animal-like robots, the “advanced robotic devices” category casts a much wider net. If a device checks these boxes, it qualifies for the ban,:

It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.
It can move, navigate or avoid obstacles on its own.
It operates remotely, either through human control or by responding to sensor data.
The device (plus any docking station) weighs more than 4.4 pounds combined.

It has a sensor that reads its surroundings, can connect to a network at 200 kbps or faster, or runs software — including AI or machine-learning models — that controls how it moves, senses its environment or receives remote commands.

Sounds like your vacuum, right? That’s because it probably is. Most robot vacuums move around on their own, connect to your Wi-Fi, gather data about your home’s layout and many weigh in above that 4.4-pound threshold. Put it all together, and they check enough boxes to land on the list.

If your robot vacuum is already part of your cleaning routine, take a breath: It’s not going to stop working, and no one’s coming to confiscate it. The ban only applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices — but since so many robot vacuums are made (or built with components made) outside the U.S., that covers the vast majority of what’s currently on the market. The key word there is new. For now, you can still buy any of the existing models that are already available at retailers.
Robot vacuums you can still shop

As mentioned, the existing inventory of robot vacuums in the United States are still up for grabs. With that in mind, I’ve rounded up robot vacuums that are still available to shop today — some are even on sale (at the time of publishing).
Eufy X10 Pro Omni

NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez tested this model as a first-time robot vacuum owner and says it took him just about 15 minutes to understand how everything worked. The robot vacuums and mops, while its base station empties debris, dumps dirty water, refills clean water, dries mop pads and recharges the battery on its own. It also offers advanced navigation, obstacle avoidance, room mapping, no-go zones and customizable routines through the Eufy app.
Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner

The Lefant M210 is a compact vacuum built for small spaces and homes with pets. At 11 inches in diameter and less than 3 inches tall, it easily cleans under beds, sofas and other low furniture. Instead of a traditional roller brush, it uses a suction port that pulls in pet hair and dirt without the tangling that roller brushes are prone to. It also offers six cleaning modes, infrared sensors to navigate around furniture and avoid falls, and app, Alexa or Google Assistant controls. When the battery runs low, it automatically returns to its charging dock, making it a low-maintenance option for everyday upkeep.
Roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum

The Roborock Q7 L5 vacuums and mops your floors at the same time, using strong suction to pull dirt out of carpets and crevices while a laser mapping system helps it find the most efficient path around your home. It’s built with anti–tangle brushes meant to resist hair wrapping, so you don’t have to clean them out as often, and the mop pads can clean dried-on stains from floors. You can use the app to set cleaning schedules and pick which rooms the vac should avoid.
iRobot Roomba 105 Vac Robot Vacuum

The iRobot Roomba 105 Vac cleans your floors on its own, using much stronger suction than older Roomba models, plus a brush along the edges and a main brush pick up different kinds of dirt. It uses laser mapping to scan and remember the layout of your home, so it can clean more thoroughly instead of bumping around randomly. You can control it through an app, which lets you schedule cleanings, focus on specific rooms and skip others.

Type: There are four main types of hair rinses: acidic, vinegar, glosses and glazes, and herbal and botanical. Each serves a different purpose, and the one you choose depends on your specific scalp or hair concern. In this list, I included options across all four types.
What is a hair rinse?

A hair rinse is a liquid treatment you’ll usually use after shampooing to address hair or scalp concerns, such as buildup, dullness, or scalp imbalance. You pour or spray the rinse over your hair and scalp, let it sit briefly and then rinse out. What makes hair rinses stand out is their consistency and contact time: “Rinses are thin, they move through the hair quickly, and they are designed to make a chemical adjustment rather than deposit a lot of product,” says Harris-Burke.

Unlike shampoo, which cleanses, or conditioner, which moisturizes and detangles, a hair rinse provides an additional targeted benefit; some rinses focus on the scalp, while others improve the look and feel of your hair shaft, says Foad.

“A hair rinse is more of a supportive product,” says Parikh. “It can help remove buildup, rebalance the scalp or improve the condition of the hair itself. It’s not a treatment for hair loss, but maintaining a healthy scalp creates a better environment for healthy hair over time.”
What are the different types of hair rinses?

There are multiple types of hair rinses, each serving a different purpose. “It’s less about choosing the trendiest product and more about choosing the one that addresses your specific scalp or hair concerns,” says Parikh.
These are the four main types of hair rinses, according to experts:

Acidic rinses (pH balancing): These have acids like citric, lactic or glycolic to lower your hair’s pH after shampooing and help lay the cuticle flat, making it appear shinier, says Harris. Acidic rinses are best for anyone with high-porosity hair, especially those with frizz, dullness or breakage. “This is the most universally useful category,” says Harris.Vinegar rinses: You’ll often see these as apple cider vinegar rinses, which have acetic acid. “They lower pH, dissolve buildup and get rid of hard water minerals,” says Harris. They’re best for people dealing with heavy product buildup, hard water or an oily, congested scalp. The trade-off is the strong smell, and the acidity means you’ll need to dilute it properly and use it less frequently, experts say.Glosses and glazes: These are semi-permanent cuticle treatments that add shine and, in tinted versions, deposit temporary color. They’re great if your hair looks dull or if you want to refresh your color between salon visits, says Harris. Clear or sheer versions give you the shine benefit without any color change, which makes them a great option for natural hair.Herbal and botanical rinses: This is the gentlest hair rinse category and the one you can typically use more frequently. They’re usually infused with rosemary, nettle, horsetail, chamomile, hibiscus, green tea or rice water, and they work to support your scalp and soothe irritation. Herbal and botanical rinses are also great for those with sensitive scalps who can’t tolerate an acidic rinse.

What are the benefits of hair rinses for different hair types?
Most hair rinses are great for any hair type, as long as you’re using the proper one for your specific concerns. Here are a few common hair types and how each benefits from a hair rinse:

Color-treated hair: Choose carefully. Strong vinegar and clarifying rinses can pull color and make it fade faster, so consider a gentle acidic rinse and gloss instead. “Glosses in particular can extend the life of your color between appointments,” says Harris.Dry, damaged hair: Acidic rinses are especially useful. “Damaged hair has a compromised cuticle that sits raised, so a pH-lowering rinse makes a visible difference,” says Harris. “Just avoid over-clarifying because damaged hair has less margin for error.”Curly and coily hair: This hair type usually benefits the most from clarifying hair rinses. “Textured hair is prone to buildup from gels, creams and butters, and buildup is one of the main reasons curls stop clumping and defining well,” says Harris. “A clarifying or chelating rinse every few weeks can reset your hair. What are the best ingredients to look for in a hair rinse?
Here are the most effective ingredients to consider for the most common hair and scalp concerns, according to Harris:

If flaking continues, that’s a sign to see a professional rather than keep switching products.For thinning hair: rosemary extract, peppermint, caffeine and niacinamide. “Rosemary in particular has some of the more encouraging research behind it, though I always frame it as scalp support rather than a cure,” says Harris. However, it’s important to have realistic expectations: “These products can support healthy hair and scalp care, but they’re not substitutes for evidence-based treatments when someone is experiencing true hair loss,” says Parikh.
For dryness and porosity: panthenol, glycerin, aloe, hydrolyzed rice or wheat protein, and amino acids.

Those with color-treated hair should look for labels like “color-safe” and “sulfate-free.” Most people with color-treated hair prefer glosses or gentle acidic rinses over strong vinegar formulas, says Harris
Frequently asked questions

While the benefits of a hair rinse depend on its ingredients, they can usually help remove buildup from your shampoo or other styling products, smooth the hair cuticle to increase shine, make your strands more manageable and support a healthier scalp environment, says Foad. Some rinses also help rebalance the scalp’s pH after cleansing, which may reduce irritation and leave hair looking smoother.
You can think of using a hair rinse almost like cleaning your kitchen, says Christine McMillan, a board-certified trichologist and owner of Scalp Garden.

“Shampoo is like washing the dishes: Its entire job is to get rid of grease, dirt and leftovers. Conditioner is like putting oil on your wooden cutting board so it stays smooth and doesn’t dry out. A hair mask is like deep conditioning that cutting board overnight; it’s meant to do more heavy lifting versus everyday maintenance,” says McMillan. “A rinse is different and more like a specialty cleaner. Maybe you’re trying to remove hard water spots, polish stainless steel or disinfect a countertop. Hair rinses are designed to do one particular job after shampooing. Some focus on your hair, some your scalp, and some do a little of both.”

In most cases, you should use a hair rinse alongside a conditioner rather than replacing it. “A rinse may help clarify the scalp or smooth the hair, but it doesn’t typically provide the level of hydration, lubrication or detangling that a conditioner does,” says Foad. “If your hair is very fine, you may find that certain hydrating rinses are sufficient on occasion, but most people benefit from using both.”
Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to correctly use a hair rinse, according to Harris:
Shampoo first. “A rinse works best on clean hair because applying it over dirt and product means it spends its energy on the residue instead of your hair,” says Harris.
Squeeze out excess water. Soaking wet hair dilutes the rinse and reduces its effectiveness.

Apply strategically. For scalp-specific rinses, use an applicator bottle with a nozzle tip to apply it, which lets you part your hair and get the product directly on your scalp where you need it, says Harris. If your rinse is made for strands, pour or spray from the mid-shaft to your ends and work it through with your fingers.

Follow the directions carefully. “Most rinses need two to five minutes. Longer is not better, especially with acidic formulas,” says Harris. “Also, if the label tells you to dilute, dilute, and do not eyeball it. Concentration matters.”
Rinse with cool water. Cool water helps the cuticle close, locking in the smoothing effect.
Follow your rinse with a conditioner unless the product specifies otherwise.

If you’re experiencing significant scalp irritation, persistent itching, painful scalp lesions, excessive hair shedding or a diagnosed scalp condition, you should speak with a dermatologist before trying any new treatments, says Foad. “These symptoms may indicate an underlying medical condition that requires evaluation rather than simply changing hair care products,” she says.

A homemade herbal or rice water rinse is a growing medium for bacteria and mold, so make small batches, refrigerate them, use them within a few days, and never keep a batch sitting on your shelf, says Harris. There is also very little consistency: “You don’t know the actual pH of what you mixed, which makes it hard to troubleshoot when something goes wrong,” says Harris.

Dilution is extremely important, and undiluted apple cider vinegar on the scalp is far too acidic and can cause irritation and cuticle damage, says Harris. If you insist on a DIY journey, a safe starting point is one to two tablespoons of apple cider vinegar in about sixteen ounces of water, she says.

Fermented rice water is a very popular DIY option right now, but you should tread carefully. “Overuse can leave hair stiff and protein overloaded, and low porosity hair is the most vulnerable to that,” says Harris. “This is also the DIY that takes the most work since traditional fermentation runs for days before the batch is usable.”

title: After Landing ‘Rockford Files’ Reboot Role, David Boreanaz Asked James Garner’s Daughter for Her Blessing
summary: David Boreanaz shared what he told James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, after he was cast to lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files.”
story: When David Boreanaz learned he would lead NBC’s reboot of “The Rockford Files,” he knew he had to reach out to James Garner’s daughter, Gigi Garner, to receive her “blessing.”

The 57-year-old actor has been a constant on network television for decades, with starring roles on “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” “Angel,” “Bones” and “SEAL Team.” But soon he will take on a new challenge as he inherits James Garner’s iconic role of Jim Rockford, a Los Angeles private investigator who relies on unconventional means to solve his crimes. James Garner, who died on July 19, 2014 at the age of 86, played the character on the original NBC series for six seasons from 1974 to 1980.

At NBC’s Backlot Pass 2026 event on Aug. 10 previewing the network and Peacock’s fall and midseason lineup, Boreanaz spoke about being inspired by the late actor, which made him want to contact Gigi Garner to assure her that her father’s legacy was in good hands.
During a panel conversation with “The Rockford Files” writer and executive producer Mike Daniels, Boreanaz explained how he got in touch with Gigi Garner to inform her of the casting news.

He said he has known the author and singer for over 15 years. He previously purchased a pinball machine from her that was a prop on her father’s show “Maverick.” But, the two had lost touch over the years. After landing the role, he found Gigi Garner’s old email address and decided to send her a message.
“I was like, I’m just going to give it a shot. I sent the email out and, to my surprise, she replied back. And I said, ‘I have to have a conversation with you,’” he recalled.
They chatted on the phone and he told her about the reboot.

“And she said, ‘Yeah, OK. I don’t know who’s going to play my father.’ And I said, ‘Well, they offered me the role,’” he continued. “And the first thing I said to her is, ‘A, I need your blessing. But first and foremost, I’m not going to play what your father did. What your father did is iconic and he’s already climbed that mountaintop. I inspire to do the same with this character, but I’m not imitating him.’”
In fact, Boreanaz told the panel audience that he didn’t grow up a fan of “The Rockford Files” and had never seen an episode.
He emphasized to Gigi Garner that he only had one goal: to make her dad proud.
“That’s it. Simple and clean and do the work,” he told her.
After they hung up, he said he went for a swim and thanked James Garner.

“I know that he’s with us. I know that he was with us in the pilot. I understand that’s a little too esoteric to think of, but that’s who I am as a person. I believe in that. I believe (the) universe has brought us to this specific moment and I do believe he’s with us,” he shared.

Another important figure in Boreanaz’s life who he has been thinking about as he enters the next chapter of his career is his mother. He said a “piece of him” owes the “Rockford” role to her because she pointed out the “uncanny” resemblance between him and James Garner years ago.
Boreanaz shared that when he was working on “Bones” his mother told him he needed to find a project connected to “The Great Escape” star.
“My mother’s spirit obviously brought that to light, somehow. So I thank my mom a little bit for that energy,” he added.
While executive producer Daniels also noted the similarities between Boreanaz and James Garner, he said the two share more characteristics that made him the perfect actor for the reboot.

“David obviously has a resemblance to Garner, but there are moments in this pilot and moments when we were on set shooting it that he would suddenly look in the camera and it was just uncanny,” Daniels said. “It wasn’t just the features. It was the half smile, the charm, the smirk, the twinkle behind the eye. It just suddenly all fit.”

He added, “Certainly, when we cast him, we were like, ‘Oh, great. He even kind of looks like the guy,’ you know. And then he got on set and we were like, ‘Whoa, he feels like the guy too in how he’s inhabiting this character.”

NBC announced it greenlit a contemporary reboot of “The Rockford Files” with Boreanaz in a press release in May. The show is expected to premiere in January 2027, with an exact date to be announced this fall. Joining Boreanaz will be Academy Award nominee Jacki Weaver, Michaela McManus and Felix Solis.

The logline for the series will sound familiar to fans of the original: “Newly paroled after doing time for a crime he didn’t commit, James Rockford returns to his life as a private investigator using his charm and wit to solve cases around Los Angeles. It doesn’t take long for his quest for legitimacy to land him squarely in the crosshairs of both local police and organized crime.”
However, Daniels clarified at the panel that the show will not be a “one‑for‑one, apples‑to‑apples remake.”

“I think you can kind of get in trouble with people who are sentimental with the original. It just becomes a comparison: who is the actor they remember loving as a kid and who’s the actor playing it now,” he explained.
Instead, he said he hopes to recapture the feeling fans experienced when they watched the classic.

title: Sugarland Is Taking Breakout Album ‘Enjoy the Ride’ Back on Tour for 20th Anniversary
summary: Sugarland is hitting the road for their “Ride Or Die Tour” for a very special reason: the 20th anniversary of their breakout album “Enjoy the Ride.”
story: Sugarland is hitting the road for a very special reason.
To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their hit album “Enjoy the Ride,” the country duo is heading out on tour this fall.

On Aug. 11, Jennifer Nettles and Kristian Bush sat down with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to discuss their exciting announcement and give a preview of what fans can expect from the aptly named the “Ride Or Die Tour.”

Nettles and Bush will be touring cities across the country from Oct. 1 to Nov. 21 to celebrate the album that solidified their spot as country icons. The official Instagram account for the duo released the official lineup of dates Aug. 11. Ticket presale begins Aug. 12 at 10 a.m. followed by general onsale Aug. 14.

Following its 2006 release, “Enjoy the Ride” went triple platinum. Throughout their time as a band, Sugarland has sold nearly 10 million albums in the U.S. The duo has won two Grammy Awards,  five ACM Awards and five consecutive CMA Awards for vocal duo of the year, from 2007 to 2011.
Nettles specifically points to “Enjoy the Ride” as a “turning point” in their career.
“Our debut album was great, but then this (was) really like when people started to really catch on to what we were doing and like it,” she said.

Bush said the album holds a special place in Sugarland’s heart since it was the first one they produced together. Outside of the band, Bush himself has produced an endless amount of music for other artists.
“Dreaming up how things sound and how they feel, it’s something I’ve been doing my whole life,” he said.
Looking back on their band’s enduring success, Nettles said she has “so much gratitude,” and Bush echoed her sentiments.
After collaborating for several decades, Bush and Nettles have a simple secret for forming a successful working relationship that lasts.

“I think like any relationship, you keep it fresh and you communicate. It doesn’t matter if it’s family. It doesn’t matter if it’s intimate. It doesn’t matter if it’s creative. Whatever, like keep it fresh. We do obviously other things. Kristian’s a fantastic producer (and) has hit records out the wazoo with Megan Moroney right now,” Nettles said.
Bush added that he and Nettles are a “unique duo” for one particular reason.

“Almost every single time we’ve sat down to do anything, maybe even in the dressing room before we walked up here, we will come up with ideas on the spot that work almost every time. And I don’t know what that (is), you know, I grab onto her,” he said.

Before announcing their new tour, Sugarland teased some exciting news on their Instagram account, posting a video of the country duo taking a bow on stage. The band captioned the post, “It’s been a minute...” and added the words “Coming soon” to the end of the video.

The day before announcing their tour, Sugarland shared another video of Nettles and Bush performing. As a plethora of excited fan comments appeared in the video, the words “We hear you!” could be seen at the end of the short clip.
Sugarland added fuel to the fire, captioning the post, “Don’t miss out...”

Sugarland released their last album in 2018 with “Bigger,” reuniting after going on hiatus starting in 2012. Nettles and Bush last toured together as Sugarland in 2024, co-headlining the “Take Me Home Tour” with Little Big Town.

title: QVC’s Toni Brattin Says She ‘Froze’ After That Viral Mishap: ‘I Just Went Down!’
summary: Jimmy Fallon had a visit from QVC wig mogul Tami Brattin days after her viral moment.
story: Jimmy Fallon’s comedic take on a viral QVC on-air moment has viewers wigging out.
The host of “The Tonight Show” welcomed TV personality Toni Brattin to his show Aug. 10 and spoofed an embarrassing moment she experienced during a recent QVC segment.
In case you missed the hilarious moment, Brattin was showcasing her collection of wigs on air when she accidentally made a NSFW reference.
While describing the wig she was wearing, Brattin said, “It looks like you went and got a blowjob.” She quickly self-corrected, saying, “a blowout at your salon.”
Terri Conn, a QVC host who was also present for the segment, quickly intervened and reminded viewers that they could take advantage of a “huge beauty sale.”
As Conn began to speak, Brattin shook her head and lowered herself to the floor, out of the camera frame.

After viewing the awkward on-air moment, Fallon poked fun at it during an episode of “The Tonight Show” last week, saying, “Note to all the married men out there: The wig is only available on your birthday, apparently.”
When Brattin saw the clip, she applauded Fallon for his witty comment during an interview with TMZ.

“Jimmy, hat’s off. I had to laugh at him as much as I had to laugh at myself. I happened to save one of those wigs just for Jimmy and I would love to see what this wig would look like on Jimmy. So Jimmy, you just tell me when your birthday is and I’ll hand deliver this and we’ll see how cute you look in it,” she said.
Brattin kept her promise and appeared on “The Tonight Show” Aug. 10.
Fallon set the scene for the segment, saying, “My birthday is actually coming up.”
Brattin then appeared and waved a brown wig in the air.
“I think that you handled that perfectly, by the way. You really nailed it,” Fallon told Brattin of her viral moment.
The TV host then asked the QVC personality what she was thinking as she slowly sank out of the camera frame after her on-air flub.
“Well, you know, I was kind of froze(n) and I was trying to decide, ‘Do I go to the left? Do I go to the right?’ I just went down,” she said.
Brattin then showed Fallon the brown wig she selected for him and put it on his head.
“Oh, look at all that hair!” she said.
“Yeah, you love it?” Fallon replied.
“And how about the volume in the back?” she added.
“Oh yeah. I love it,” Fallon said, then posed. “I’m honored. I love it.”
Brattin paused to fluff up the wig a bit then covered her face and laughed as Fallon exclaimed, “I am blown away.”
The duo ended the segment by turning their backs to the camera and lowering their bodies as they introduced “The Tonight Show” house band, The Roots.

title: Usher Responds to Rumors as Fans Believe He’s Hired a Look-Alike to Perform at Concerts
summary: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
story: Usher is shutting down rumors that he’s been sending out an imposter to perform in his place during his recent joint tour with Chris Brown.
Fans have been doing double takes for days after footage from a recent “The R&B Tour” concert has convinced many of them that the man performing on stage was a fake.

Sunnya Sultan, who saw the tour in person Aug. 7 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, shared a TikTok video questioning if the 47-year-old “Yeah” singer was truly the one dancing in front of her.
The performer wears a white with lime green and pink ensemble, ball cap and sunglasses as he sings and dances.
Sultan tells TODAY.com she believes she did see Usher perform. She’s also convinced an Usher look-alike also took the stage during a portion of the show.

“Usher came out. The real Usher came out but then he sang like half a song, maybe for like 40 seconds,” Sultan recalls. “Then he goes into this darkness and he comes out, and as he’s walking, I think everyone really thought that was Usher.”
“But as the first song finishes, I think everyone started getting confused because the way he was moving wasn’t really Usher,” she continues.

When she looked closely, she believed something was off about the Usher who now appeared onstage. She noted that his jawline that was “a little too chiseled” and the performer “seemed a little too stiff.”
Also, he was dressed differently. The “real” Usher, she says, came out shirtless and wearing a fur coat.
The Usher who later performed in front of her, she adds, was “fully covered,” as seen in her TikTok video.
“Everything was just kind of weird,” Sultan says. “He looked like him, and then at certain angles he definitely did not look like him.”
Sultan said concertgoers all around her were suspicious.
Usher addressed the rumors in a video posted on the tour’s official Instagram Aug. 9.
“Usure? Wesure,” reads the caption.
The video showed Usher performing onstage in the same white ensemble. It also included screenshots of Usher replying to comments made about the alleged imposter.
“Ya’ll are funny…clone? They can’t clone this??” the singer wrote alongside a laughing emoji.
“How ya’ll come up with this? AI ain’t that advanced,” he added along with more laughing emoji.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Has Shocking Elimination After Dancer Failed to Deliver ‘Wow Moment’
summary: Who was eliminated on ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ episode 5? The Aug. 10 episode saw a shocking elimination after one dancer failed to deliver a “wow moment.”
story: The competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro” and now it’s time to shine.
In the Aug. 10 episode of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff, pro Daniella Karagach showed off her impressive skills with a mega performance as host Robert Irwin introduced the challenge.

This week it was all about having that “wow” moment that “DWTS” viewers love. The six remaining dancers were mentored and guided by Daniella as they created a contemporary routine that incorporated one of her signature and viral moves.
If the dancers failed to deliver a spectacular move in their choreographer, they would be at risk for elimination. But first, the contestants took a trip to the Australia Zoo for inspiration.
What Happened During Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’

When Daniella entered the rehearsal room, she told the dancers that they also had to create their own standout moment that would “forever be embedded in someone’s memory.” This was in addition to including one of Daniella’s “wow” moves.
“The more you wow the audience, the longer you and your partner stay in the competition,” she said about competing on “DWTS.”

Since last week, the ladies got to choose their partners, this week the guys picked who they wanted to perform with. If more than one guy chose the same girl, she would have the option to choose who she wanted to partner up with.
Allen Genkin chose Adele Zaikman, while AJ Pritchard and Erik Linder chose Selena Hamilton. No one chose Nina Mayster.
Selena ultimately chose Erik, meaning AJ and Nina would be partners by default.

AJ and Nina were up first, performing a contemporary piece to “Human” by Christina Perri that impressed the judges. Daniella told them they “understood the assignment,” while judge Mark Ballas complimented their “total trust.”
Shirley Ballas also applauded their multiple wow moments, AJ’s vulnerability and Nina’s musicality.
Next were Allen and Adele, who also got major kudos from the judges with their routine to “All That Really Matters” by Illenium featuring Teddy Swims.
Mark was a fan of their wow moments, that included the Allen-copter and caveman walk at the beginning. He also called Adele a “diamond.”
Shirley echoed her son’s comments, calling her “beyond a diamond, one of the best female dancers I’ve ever seen.” Daniella also shared how she loved the routine.
Last but not least were Erik and Selena, who specializes in contemporary, with a routine to “You Stole the Show” by Sienna Spiro.
Shirley began her comments by saying she was “conflicted” and didn’t know what their wow moment was. Selena replied that sometimes the “wow” is in the silence.
Shirley continued by saying she would have liked to see Erik let go more and ultimately wasn’t impressed. While she did appreciate the quality of Selena’s routine, she expected more.
Mark and Daniella both shared kind words about their dancing, but noted that they did not follow direction.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?
Because they did not complete the challenge and include a visibly “wow moment” in their routine, Erik and Selena were on the chopping block.
The other four contestants were visibly emotional in the background, as Daniella said, “If you have a challenge, you have to deliver it. You have to make that the priority.”
Who Got Eliminated on Episode 5 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?
Ultimately, Shirley shared that with a “very, very heavy heart” this would be the last dance for Erik.
Allen broke down in tears, with Adele and Nina covering their faces in shock.
Shirley told Erik that he was “a beautiful dancer,” but applauded Selena for her strong and advanced choreography.

“I knew that I was taking a risk,” Erik said in his confessional, adding that he didn’t regret a single decision that he made. He then thanked the judges for the opportunity to grow as a dancer and person.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Five dancers remain on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” For the Aug. 17 episode, guest judge Witney Carson will deliver the dancers’ toughest challenge yet: teaching ballroom novice.
In the next episode, the contestants will be paired with “DWTS” superfans who are dancing amateurs. They will then have two days to prepare a performance that will land them a spot in the semifinals.

title: Brad Pitt Makes Rare Comment About ‘Pain’ of ‘Family Stuff’
summary: In a new interview, Brad Pitt shares that he’s never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”
story: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
In a rare mention of his personal life, Brad Pitt says in a new interview that he has never been suicidal “except for one little period” that was related to “family stuff.”

The 62-year-old Hollywood icon made a short reference to his family situation in an interview with Esquire published on Aug. 10  in which he talked about “oppressive” pain that led him to a dark place where he could “understand suicide.”
In the Esquire interview, Pitt initially shared his thoughts about going to dark places in life, unconnected to any question about his family.
“I was never suicidal in any way,” he said. “It just was not my makeup. In fact, if I have any afflictions, it’s probably being a congenital optimist,” he said.
He reiterated he’s “never been suicidal,” before adding, “except for one little period.”

“And in that one little period, I just thought — I just couldn’t — just didn’t see a way out,” he said. “The pain was so oppressive that — I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel — I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief. And I thought, Oh, okay, now I understand — I understand suicide, in the sense that it’s just relief. It’s just looking for relief from the pain. But I also think we have incredible survival instincts. And for me, that immediately kicked in, but it was just ...”
Pitt was asked what could have provoked him to think about suicide in that way. The reporter questioned if it was “kid stuff,” per the Esquire article.
“Family stuff,” Pitt said. “We could leave it at that.”

Pitt and his ex-wife, Angelina Jolie, have six children. The couple reached a divorce settlement in 2024 after Jolie accused Pitt of verbal and physical abuse, which he has denied. Their daughter Shiloh, 20, legally dropped “Pitt” from her last name when she turned 18 in 2024. Two of his other children have also considered ditching “Pitt” from their last name, according to a court filing in California cited by CNN in July 2026.
The “F1” star was later asked how he endured the difficult period he referenced.

“I don’t see it as climbing out of it,” he said. “It’s going through it and trying and trying and trying and trying to the point of exhaustion and then trying again. I don’t want to ignore the place where you run up against the wall. But I just one day woke up, and it just felt a little sunnier and the air felt a little sweeter. Just microdoses of it.”

Pitt does not make it clear in the interview what “little period” he is referring to in his life. Elsewhere in the interview, he discussed the death of his mother in August 2025 and said, referencing his father, “Let’s just say it’s better to be the one who goes first.”
Once Hollywood’s most famous couple, Pitt, and Jolie, 51, met on the set of the 2005 movie “Mr. & Mrs. Smith” and got married in 2014. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016.

In 2022, amid already contentious divorce proceedings, Jolie accused Pitt of physical and verbal abuse on a 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles, during which he allegedly choked one of their children, which prompted her to file for divorce, according to a court filing from Jolie.
“Brad has owned everything he’s responsible for from day one — unlike the other side — but he’s not going to own anything he didn’t do,” a lawyer for Pitt said in 2022.

No criminal charges were ever filed against Pitt. In 2016, both the FBI and the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services closed an investigation into allegations of abuse onboard the flight.

The acrimony since their split has also included Pitt filing a lawsuit in 2022 accusing Jolie of intentionally harming him and the French winery business they once shared by selling her stake in it. The former couple purchased shares in the 148-acre French vineyard Chateau Miraval together in 2008.

Following Pitt’s lawsuit about the winery, Jolie filed the 2022 cross-complaint that alleged Pitt subjected their family to verbal and physical abuse aboard the aforementioned 2016 flight from France to Los Angeles.
Their divorce was settled in 2024, and the dispute over the winery remains ongoing.

title: Romy Reiner’s Latest TV Role Has a Touching Tie to Her Late Dad, Rob Reiner
summary: Romy Reiner appeared in the finale of Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness,” which her dad Rob Reiner also appeared in.
story: Romy Reiner followed in her late father Rob Reiner’s footsteps by appearing on Larry David’s “Life, Larry, and the Pursuit of Unhappiness.”
The elder Reiner made a posthumous cameo in the sketch show in an episode that aired July 3, months after his shocking death. He played George Washington.
Romy Reiner, meanwhile, guest-starred in the series finale on Aug. 7 as a nurse caring for President William Henry Harrison (Fred Melamed).
Romy Reiner’s appearance comes five years after she got her big break in 2021 playing a cashier on David’s HBO series “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” David was one of Rob Reiner’s close friends.
The 28-year-old actor is the youngest child of the legendary actor and director and his late wife Michele Singer.
The couple, who were married for 36 years, were found fatally stabbed at home on Dec. 14, 2025, according to the L.A. district attorney’s office.
Their youngest son, Nick Reiner, 32, was arrested and charged Dec. 16 with two counts of first degree murder. In February, Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The Reiners also shared an older son, Jake Reiner, 35, who posted a heartbreaking tribute to his parents in an April 24 post on Substack.
Rob Reiner was also the father of an adoptive daughter, Tracy Reiner, with his ex-wife, actor and director Penny Marshall.
In his essay on Substack, Jake Reiner revealed he was at a friend’s celebration of life in Los Angeles when his sister called to tell him their parents were dead.

“The 45-minute Lyft ride from downtown to the west side was unendurable,” he wrote. “My world, as I knew it, had collapsed. I was in a trance. The only thing I could focus on was that I needed to get to my childhood home. I needed to get to my sister. I needed to figure out what the hell just happened.”
Jake Reiner wrote about his grief that his parents won’t be alive to witness future milestones in his life.

“My parents won’t be at my wedding, they won’t get to hold their future grandchild, and they won’t get to see me have the successful career I’m still seeking,” he wrote. “It simultaneously breaks my heart and enrages me.”
Rob Reiner, who was 78 when he died, was the son of comedy legend Carl Reiner. He found fame in the early 1970s playing Michael “Meathead” Stivic on the sitcom “All in the Family.”

He went on to become one of Hollywood’s most beloved directors, helming the cult classic “This Is Spinal Tap” as well as the box office hits “Stand By Me,” “The Princess Bride,” “When Harry Met Sally,” “Misery” and “A Few Good Men.”
He married photographer and producer Michele Reiner in May 1989.
In his essay, Jake Reiner called his parents “the most giving people.” He described his father as his “hero” and Singer as “the backbone” of the family.
Losing his parents together in such a violent manner — with his brother “at the center of it” — has been, he wrote, a “living nightmare.”

title: New Yorker Accidentally Threw Away 2 Family Rings. 20,000 Pounds of Trash Later, They Were Recovered
summary: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
story: New York City sanitation workers dug through 20,000 pounds of garbage to ensure that one man’s trash didn’t also mean the loss of his treasure.
A Brooklyn man is breathing a massive sigh of relief after he accidentally threw a pair of priceless family rings in the garbage at a large residential building last month.

The ring’s owner realized the mistake before the trash was picked up, so he met sanitation workers at the curb on July 28 to explain the predicament, a spokesperson for the New York City Department of Sanitation told TODAY.com in an email statement.
The heirloom rings were a gold-and-diamond promise ring and platinum-and-diamond engagement ring that had been in the family for four generations, according to the DSNY.

Sanitation workers were able to isolate the truck and slowly dump the nearly 20,000 pounds of trash across a concrete floor to be searched. After only 10 minutes, the rings were found to the relief and joy of the resident, whose name was withheld by the DSNY.
“It isn’t exactly a needle in a haystack, but some accidentally discarded rings were dug up!,” the DSNY wrote on Facebook.
“Can you imagine?” Savannah Guthrie said on TODAY Aug. 10. “Out of the goodness of their hearts being like, ‘I’m going to sift through 20,000 pounds of trash,’ and they found it! Incredible.”
The DSNY spokesperson said searches like that happen multiple times a year, and there is a process for them.

Any residents who accidentally throw out a valuable item are urged to call 311 as soon as possible. After each call, sanitation workers aim to isolate the truck and slowly dump the contents on a concrete floor to be sifted through.

The timeliness of the call is crucial. If a truck has already dumped the trash at a transfer station, there’s no way to recover the lost item because it’s usually immediately mixed with trash from other trucks to be put into a barge or railcar.

The resident is allowed to participate in the search for his or her item and can bring one friend to help. The DSNY provides gloves, shovels, pickers and other tools for the search while also sharing possible spots to look. For instance, if the person’s address was at the beginning of the sanitation truck’s route, the material may be more near the back of the truck.
The recovery of the Brooklyn man’s rings is the latest success story for the DSNY, which has previously found everything from a wallet to a laptop that had been accidentally tossed out.
“Way to go New York City Sanitation,” Craig Melvin said on TODAY.

title: Anthony Bourdain’s Daughter Was A ‘Brutal’ Critic About His Cooking, He Joked In 2016 on TODAY
summary: In 2016, Anthony Bourdain sat down with TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on how he got into TV, his experiences traveling the world and cooking for his daughter.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Anthony Bourdain’s conversation with Willie Geist on Oct. 23, 2016.
The legacy of Anthony Bourdain lives on with the release of “Tony,”
In the film, out now, Dominic Sessa plays the celebrated and complicated chef, who died in 2018 at the age of 61 by suicide, leaving behind a legion of fans who are still inspired by him.

In 2016, Bourdain sat down with Sunday TODAY’s Willie Geist to reflect on his career, remembering how he wound up a fixture of the small screen, what it was like to eat with the president and how his toughest critic may be his daughter.
How Did Anthony Bourdain Break Into Show Business?

Bourdain shot to stardom after he wrote the 2000 book “Kitchen Confidential,” which, based on his experience, took readers behind the scenes of the restaurant industry. It also touched on his personal struggles with addiction.
