“I wrote an article,” he told Willie at the time. “My mom actually said, ‘You should send it to the New Yorker.’”
“The next day I got a call saying, ‘You know, we’ll give you 50 grand to write a book,’” he recalled. “I’m no dummy, I’m dunking french fries at age 44. I’ll write the d--- book.”
What Was Next for Bourdain After That?

The next stop was television. Following stints on the Travel Channel and Food Network, Bourdain turned his success into the long-running TV series “Parts Unknown,” in which he dove into the food of obscure places around the globe.

“Some delusional crackpots walked into the restaurant and offered me a TV show, and they showed up reeking of garlic, with a really bad attitude,” he recalled about how he wound up making shows about food and travel.

“I said, ‘I got a great idea. I travel around the world doing whatever I want in every cool place I ever dreamed of, and you pay. How’s that idea?’” he said. “And they were like, ‘Sounds like ... yeah. We’ll take 13 (episodes) of those.”
Bourdain Was Curious About Traveling Around the World
Bourdain was not afraid to get out of his comfort zone when it came to where he would visit.
“I’m not going full Geraldo (Rivera) out there in my flak jacket, poking my head up over a foxhole,” he said.
“But, you know, I’m curious about the world. And if there are manageable risks in return for satisfying my curiosity about a place, I’m willing,” he shared.
He Ate With Former President Barack Obama
Bourdain did sit down once with Barack Obama while he was president and remembered how he handled a potentially tricky question when he asked Obama how he felt about eating a hot dog with ketchup.

“Most people running for office would say, ‘Both ketchup and mustard, there are virtues, and I respect and admire people who...’ you know, get some wishy-washy answer to not piss off all the ketchup people. He said, ‘No, never!’” Bourdain recalled.
How Did Bourdain Choose Which Places to Spotlight?
For Bourdain, visiting an eatery, even if no one was familiar with it, came down to something very simple.

“The kind of questions we’re asking is, ‘Look, what does your soul crave at 2 o’clock in the morning when you got a little bit of a buzz?’ More often than not, that goes right to the heart of the culture,” he said.
Bourdain’s Daughter Was Not Afraid to Criticize His Cooking

Bourdain shared a daughter, Ariane, with ex-wife Ottavia Busia. She was 11 when he died, and Bourdain told Willie in their 2016 chat that she was tough as nails when it came to her reviews of his food.
“She’s brutal. I cannot get anything past her,” he said. “It’s like, ‘No, daddy, it’s too salty.’ ‘No, it’s not.’ Secretly, I know, yeah, she caught me. Every time.”
At the time, he also spoke about how his daughter inspired his new cookbook “Appetites: A Cookbook.”

title: ‘Wicker’ Movie Explained: Why Is the Internet Thirsting Over a Sentient Basket?
summary: What is the Wicker movie? Here’s the explanation of the Wicker movie, what it’s based on and the reaction to it.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the biggest headlines, leading with your questions. In this latest series, we’re breaking down why a movie about love and wicker sparked a big reaction.
The Scarecrow and the Tin Man better watch out, because there’s a new anthropomorphic leading man who has captured Hollywood’s attention … and he’s made of wicker.

Distributor Black Bear Pictures delighted and bewildered the internet on July 30 when it released the first trailer for an upcoming romantic fantasy comedy titled “Wicker,” out in theaters in the U.S. Oct. 23 and Oct. 30 in the UK. (The movie premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival in January.)

The film was first announced back in October 2023, when Variety reported that Oscar-winner Olivia Colman and Dev Patel were attached to a movie featuring an “unconventional romance.” But two years later, the publication announced Alexander Skarsgård would replace Patel, and that Peter Dinklage and Elizabeth Debicki were joining the cast, too.

A star-studded cast plus an intriguing plot seem like a recipe for a film worth checking out. But nothing could have prepared the internet for the first look, which showed Skarsgård’s full transformation into an unrecognizable man made of wicker.
Read on to find out why the internet is thirsting over Skarsgård’s twine-filled alter ego.
What Is ‘Wicker’ About?

As the film title implies, wicker is at the center of the story. The nearly two-and-a-half minute NSFW teaser that Black Bear Pictures debuted, which has already amassed over 1.5 million views, welcomes viewers to a seaside village where a fisherwoman, played by Colman, is ridiculed by members of the town.
Lonely and in need of a companion, the fisherwoman visits a local craftsman, portrayed by Dinklage, and requests that he make her a husband.
“Be at the chapel in a month,” he simply tells her.

After bending and molding endless sticks of twine, he creates her husband: Skarsgård’s wicker man. From head to toe, he is covered in wicker strands, which have been weaved and stitched together in various patterns across his body.
“I’m here to marry you,” Skarsgård’s character tells the fisherwoman upon seeing her. It’s safe to say she is pleased with the results.
The two begin their unusual love story, as some of the townspeople who previously mocked the fisherwoman now desire the same romance. Others are mortified and chaos ensues.
What Inspired ‘Wicker’?

“Wicker” was adapted from Ursula Wills-Jones’ short story “The Wicker Husband.” According to its Goodreads description, the 14-page story follows “an ugly girl who was short and dumpy, had one leg a bit shorter than the other, and her eyebrows met in the middle” — and she “wanted to marry.”
“Who will marry her while all the people made fun of her?” the premise asks. “Then, she married the wicker husband. what happened when she married him? What was the people’s reaction?”
In 2020, the story was turned into a folk musical that ran for a few weeks at the Watermill Theatre in Newbury, England.

A Facebook post from the theatre in March 2020 revealed that the production would use puppetry to bring the wicker man to life. “It is these puppets that steal the show,” recaps The Guardian’s three-star review of the show.
How Are Fans Reacting to the Trailer?
Fans’ reactions to the trailer have ranged from humorous posts about the plot to pure confusion to ... well, thirst with a side helping of surprise.
Beneath the YouTube trailer, fans left comments poking fun at the concept.
“Expected a horror film trailer, stayed for whatever this was,” one joked.
Another wrote, “Just when I think Alexander Skarsgard has finally achieved his weirdest role he comes at me with this.”
A third said, “I love that Peter Dinklage’s character is asked to make a Cottagecore Frankenstein and immediately says ‘say less.’”
Ikea joined in on the fun on Instagram by sharing a picture of a chair made of wicker with text that read “husband material.”
“We’ve got plenty of husband material,” the furniture company captioned the post before asking social media users to share how many times they watched the “Wicker” trailer.
A “Wicker” movie account responded, “No assembly required.”
To which Ikea cheekily replied, “Looking at our wicker furniture a little differently these days,” with a smirk emoji.
One Instagram user commented with an idea for the store. “And now all wicker items must be renamed to Skarsgård,” she wrote.
“Big Wick Energy,” another comment read.
Content creator JessAfterDark shared a hilarious Instagram video of her watching the trailer with her husband, who uttered, “Oh God!” when he saw Skarsgård’s character for the first time.
When the clip ended, he said he “couldn’t wait” to watch the movie.
Another Instagram user predicted that “baskets are about to make a huge comeback” on her page, adding “iykyk” (if you know you know).
In the caption she playfully wrote, “Alex Skarsgård… the basket that you are.”

title: A Hospital Patient Dreamed Of Attending A Metal Concert. So The Show Came To Him
summary: Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert but couldn’t leave the facility. So the show came to him.
story: Now *this* is metal.

Tim Berry, a 27-year-old patient at Bruyère Health in Ottawa, Canada, recently wished to attend a metal concert after receiving some difficult news about his health, clinical chaplain Roshene Lawson tells TODAY.com. While he was too medically fragile to leave the facility, Lawson pulled some strings to make magic happen.

With the help of staff and some kind folks at a local venue, Lawson threw a real metal show at the hospital in July, featuring band The Scepter, a whole lot of headbanging and, of course, that metalhead spirit.
Berry was able to rock out safely.

“Our clinical manager had told me he had some tears coming down during the concert,” Lawson says of Berry. “I went to ask him after. I said, ‘Were you crying because it was so loud?’ ... and he laughed and he said, ‘No, I’m really happy.’”

The Scepter played a 40-minute set for Berry, Lawson recounts. The band performed while fully decked out in their metal garb. They also set up their lights and blaring amps, along with some fans to blast their long locks, she says.
The Scepter’s Josh Collins explains that the band attempted to give Berry the most authentic experience they could.

“We wanted to give him a real show, not a watered down version because we were playing in a hospital,” he says. “It was emotional, for sure, but mostly we just felt privileged to be there and to play for him.”
Nurses painted Berry’s nails for the occasion and dressed him in a heavy metal shirt, Lawson adds. She even made tickets for the event, which patients used to attend the rock show.
“Everybody had to have their ticket to get in, and we tore the ticket, and they came in, and we had staff enjoying it with them,” Lawson says.

The chaplain explains that the idea for the concert came from a conversation she had with Berry after he was told about a change in his condition. She declined to disclose further medical details to protect Berry’s privacy.

“I went in and said to him, ‘Really, we can focus on this and how sad and frustrating it is, or we can focus on what you want to do with what’s left of life,’” Lawson recalls. “And he said, ‘I’d really, really like to go to a heavy metal concert.’”

Since Berry wasn’t cleared to leave the hospital, Lawson had to get creative. She called around and found Dominion Tavern, a spot that regularly hosts shows, and asked them for help. The business was more than happy to get on board, owner Scott McClinton says.
“I was in the unique position to be able to pull something like this off,” McClinton says. “I had most of the equipment, I know tons of bands and put on multiple shows weekly.”
It didn’t take long for McClinton to tap local band The Scepter for the performance, he says.

“They play straight-up epic, fun metal and always put on a great show,” McClinton says. “Plus I know a few of the members pretty well and they’re just really great, sweet dudes who I knew would say yes immediately – which was key as we didn’t have much time to organize all this.”
One of the trickiest aspects of the planning process, Lawson says, was finding the right spot to host such a raucous bash.

“It’s not quiet music, and we have other patients for whom that might not be their genre of music, so we had to find a place where we could put a proper concert on, where he could really live it as a concert,” Lawson says.
A conference room ended up being the perfect venue. And after moving around some furniture and setting up the band’s equipment, the scene was transformed, Lawson says.
“And honestly, the nurses, the recreation therapists, the physio, the OT, the clinical manager — everybody worked together to make this a fun thing for him,” Lawson adds.

While heavy metal isn’t always associated with comfort and peace, Lawson explains that it’s critical to meet patients’ unique needs. It’s especially important in a medical environment where there isn’t a lot of room to scream and shout and let it all out when you need to, she says.

“You and I could go home to our place, and if we’re having a bad day, just scream into a pillow or cry out loud or do whatever we need to do,” Lawson explains. “That’s harder to do when you’re in care.”

Lawson said that having a moment to rock out is “so cathartic, when you can really let that noise wash over you and it’s not the buzzing of the machines or the ringing of the call bells or the sound of the suction machine. It is bona fide living.”
The experience wasn’t just a memorable one for Berry. It’s also been impactful for McClinton, Lawson and all those involved.
“Getting to see Tim’s smile and the reaction from the staff is something that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” McClinton says.
He adds that “if you get a chance to help make someone’s day better, just do it.”
“It’ll be great for them and could be unbelievably rewarding for you,”  McClinton says.
The Scepter, whose members say they’ve felt moved by the concert as well, is also dedicating their next album to Berry.

“He brought us into something much bigger than we ever expected, and it feels right that he should be part of what comes next for us,” Collins says. “Dedicating the album to Tim is our way of recognizing him and what this experience has meant to the band.”
Rock on, Tim. Rock on.

title: Jason Sudeikis Shares How Ted Lasso Character Made Him A Better Dad
summary: In Apple TV’s “Ted Lasso,” the titular English football coach worships a hand-taped “Believe” sign like it’s scripture, simply cannot resist a folksy metaphor and thinks that a relentless stream of shortbread biscuits is the way to his boss’ heart.
story: In Apple TV’s “Ted Lasso,” the titular English football coach worships a hand-taped “Believe” sign like it’s scripture, simply cannot resist a folksy metaphor and thinks that a relentless stream of shortbread biscuits is the way to his boss’ heart.
For all of his quirks, Jason Sudeikis’ character Ted Lasso has taught the actor legitimate lessons about parenting, he told Willie Geist during the Aug. 9 episode of Sunday Sitdown.
“I think he’s a very sincere person, he accepts people where they are,” Sudeikis, 50, said.
“It’s made me a better parent,” he said. “I think there’s just a level of accountability that I think we love puttin’ on the show.”

After the Season 3 finale sent Ted back to Kansas City to coach his son’s team — a conclusion many viewers saw as the end of the show’s arc — Season 4 brought him right back across the pond. This time, he’s coaching a newly formed second-division women’s team.
In the new season, which premiered Aug. 5, Ted’s Lady Greyhounds encounter new challenges: sub-par facilities, less funding and skepticism toward women athletes.
Sudeikis acknowledged that “Ted Lasso” is, at its heart, a “silly fun show.” But still, its emotional resonance can carry real weight, he said.

“When a certain moment gets people and makes ‘em feel seen or it makes ‘em want to try or do something differently, it feels like a tremendous responsibility, ‘cause it’s bigger than me,” he explained.

Indeed, beneath the laughs of the first three seasons, Ted and the show’s other characters navigate mental health challenges, experience divorce and learn about what it means to actually lean on one another. The new season addresses other salient topics including the struggles that many women in sports continue to face.
Sudeikis opened up to the TODAY host about why the show pivoted to focus on a women’s team.

Production kicked around a few possibilities, he said, but nothing felt “as gooey” or “as juicy” as the storyline teased in the Season 3 finale, when a pitch for a Richmond women’s squad is first introduced.
The actor’s excitement for the show’s new twist was shaped in part by the women closest to him.
“I know how kick ass little girls are, having one of my own, but also, you know, growin’ up around a couple,” he told Willie.
He also added: “Being an older brother to two wise, funny, silly, authentic, heartfelt women, then-girls, now women — is baked into the enthusiasm for doing this new season.”

title: Chef Eric Ripert, One of Anthony Bourdain’s Closest Friends, Shares What It Was Like to Appear in ‘Tony’
summary: Eric Ripert tells TODAY.com how “Tony” portrays a different man than the public knew his late friend Anthony Bourdain to be. He also opens up about his cameo in the biopic.
story: If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

When chef Eric Ripert sat down to watch “Tony,” the biopic centered on the early life of his late close friend Anthony Bourdain, he didn’t recognize the man on the screen. He says that was a good thing.

“Tony,” out now and already lauded by critics, is a coming-of-age story, where a 19-year-old Bourdain first develops his passion for food and sense of self. The candid chef, Emmy-winning television host and bestselling author who fans all over the world adored isn’t found onscreen. Instead, Dominic Sessa portrays a young Bourdain as a rudderless teenager who dreams of being a writer and initially treats his time working in a kitchen in the Cape Cod city of Provincetown as a meaningless summer job.

Ripert, an icon in the culinary world and chef and co-owner at three-Michelin star restaurant Le Bernardin in New York City, first saw the film during a private A24 screening. He watched it again at the New York premiere on July 28. He says he was happy to see a movie about his friend, who died on June 8, 2018 at the age of 61, and was also intrigued by the entire story unfolding over one summer.

“It’s very artistic, the way they are approaching the subject of Anthony being 19 years old. The public has very little information about Anthony during that era, because he never really discussed much in public about that era,” he tells TODAY.com before referencing a chapter in Bourdain’s unfiltered memoir “Kitchen Confidential” where he writes about a summer in Provincetown. “So they had to take some creative liberties.”
Despite knowing the concept for the film, Ripert, who first met Bourdain decades after “Tony’s” setting, says he was still taken aback by this version of the chef.

“When I saw the movie for the first time, I was like, ‘Wow, this is not the Anthony that I met when I met him.’ But I met him much later on in life,” he shares. “When I met him, he wrote already ‘Kitchen Confidential.’ I was thinking to myself, ‘Oh, when I met Anthony, he was very charismatic and very secure and very friendly’ … when I saw the movie, it reminded me that when you are young and you are in your 20s, you’re searching for yourself. You’re not the same person at 20 than when you are 40 or 60 and so on.”
“When I met Anthony, he already had passed that era,” he adds.
That ’70s era of Bourdain included messy, curly hair, thick sideburns, an impulsive nature and quite a bit of dishonesty.
Ripert puts it more frankly: “What is interesting is that in the movie, he lies a lot,” he says, laughing. “He’s basically a chronic liar.”
The character Tony was the opposite of Bourdain in that sense, according to Ripert.

“What strike me about Anthony during our friendship, it was like he never lied. And I guess gaining confidence and deciding to change his life made him conscious of the fact that he was lying a lot when he was young. All those sins of lying are interesting because, again, I never saw Anthony lying. And sometimes he was brutally honest and he couldn’t lie,” says Ripert.

The drug usage in “Tony” might be jarring for some viewers, but that was a struggle of Bourdain’s that Ripert was aware of. He tells TODAY.com the two had many private discussions about Bourdain’s past with substance abuse, including heroin, which he opened up about in “Kitchen Confidential.”

Tony develops some bad habits, fueled by line cook Leo Woodall’s Sal. However, through the guidance of a patient and sagacious chef, played by Antonio Banderas, Tony begins to realize the type of man he wants to be and what matters to him.

Part of this epiphany comes in a scene featuring Ripert, who plays an admissions officer at the Culinary Institute of America. (Bourdain eventually enrolled at the institute and graduated in 1978.) Ripert’s appearance in the film was a sweet nod to his friendship with Bourdain, which fans followed for years as the French chef frequently made appearances on “No Reservations” and “Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown.”

“I was his sidekick,” Ripert says while reminiscing about the two traveling the world together. “We had a good, nice dynamic. I knew where to stand, and I knew that I was here for him to tease me, and so on. In real life, it was a lot different. We had a lot of respect (for) each other and enjoyed the friendship.”

So when Kim Witherspoon, Ripert’s agent who was also Bourdain’s agent and now represents the late chef’s estate, reached out and asked the restaurateur if he wanted to appear in the film, he jumped at the opportunity. He recalls Witherspoon, an executive producer on “Tony,” giving him few details about the film: the director, the actors involved, the basic plot and that his cameo would come at the end.
“I didn’t question it,” he says.
He describes his scene as a representation of Bourdain “closing one door and opening another one.”
“It was a turning point in his life, and I thought it was nice for me to be in that moment in a movie … (to) basically bring Tony to another direction after struggling during that summer,” he shares.
Ripert’s time on set was brief. He had a quick discussion with director Matt Johnson, who showed him around. He didn’t talk to Sessa at all the day he filmed despite them acting opposite each other.

“Dominic was in character, and it was difficult for him to get out of that character, I guess,” Ripert says. But he understands how committed Sessa was to nailing the part, and he approved of the end result.
“I think he did a great job,” Ripert says. “Because he has very little references to be Anthony.”

He continues, “It’s very credible that Anthony was like that. I’m not sure because, again, when I met Anthony, he was a very different man. But I enjoy the acting of Dominic, and I thought for a young actor like him, it’s really a powerful exercise that he did. Also, I don’t know if he felt the pressure of excelling at being Anthony and being as authentic as he could. It’s not an easy job to be Anthony Bourdain.”

Bourdain died by suicide at the Le Chambard hotel while on location in France to film an episode of “Parts Unknown.” CNN reported at the time that Ripert was the one who found his friend in his hotel room.
When Ripert and Sessa filmed their scene together, the fine dining chef became emotional. Although his cameo was only about 20 seconds, it was a powerful moment for Ripert.
“It was emotional because suddenly the camera were running, and I was (in) the front of a young Anthony Bourdain, and I believed it,” says Ripert, who is now 61, the same age when Bourdain died.
He hopes that fans of Bourdain also feel that emotional pull when they watch “Tony,” even though it might not be what they are expecting.

“I hope they will relate to Anthony, because a lot of people have seen Anthony on television. People traveled with him throughout the world week after week, every Sunday he was in your living room or in your bedroom on the TV screen. We see a very different Anthony in that movie,” Ripert says. “I hope people will understand that in his life it was an evolution. He was who he is in the movie, and then suddenly he made changes and life molded into a different character. I hope people will connect.”

title: 6 Women Who Changed TV Forever Answer 1 Question: What Makes a Good ‘Real Housewife’?
summary: Vicki Gunvalson, Luann de Lesseps, Teresa Giudice, Kyle Richards, Gizelle Bryant and Lisa Barlow speak to TODAY about what makes a good “Real Housewife.”
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Any fan of “Real Housewives” can identify the moment they watched that made them a true believer. It’s a scene that imprints so deeply, all a person can do is clutch their chest, whisper a silent prayer of gratitude and recognize oneself as changed for the better.

A lot of these moments are universally beloved, like Teresa Giudice’s table flip, or Bethenny Frankel’s “it’s about Tom,” or NeNe Leakes’ dismay over a white refrigerator, or Vicki Gunvalson and the little family van. A lot of these moments, too, are largely defined by the original “Housewives.”
In the Bravoverse, those who have been with their respective series from inception are women of legends. They are pioneers of their craft. The OGs, as they’re called. Our founding mothers.

And make no mistake, they are aware of their contributions and the trail they’ve blazed. How do we know that? Well, we at TODAY.com were able to ask some of them what they believe defines a “Real Housewife.”
“It’s a full-time occupation,” Luann said. “It really is, and one that has changed the idea of what a housewife really is.”

Luann, of “The Real Housewives of New York City,” was among six OGs who came to TODAY this week to celebrate 20 years since the original “Housewives” set in Orange County premiered in 2006. Bravo is celebrating in a big way, too, as OGs headline the fifth season of “The Real Housewives Ultimate Girls Trip,” dubbed “Roaring 20th” and premiering Aug. 9 on Bravo. The season will also feature cameos from 82 (!!) other “Housewives.”
“(It’s) the greatest trip down memory line for, what I think is, the greatest docu-soap opera in TV history,” “Real Housewives” executive producer Andy Cohen said Aug 5 on TODAY.

Below, we gave the mic to six OGs: Luann, as well as Teresa of “The Real Housewives of New Jersey,” Vicki from “The Real Housewives of Orange County,” Kyle Richards from “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills,” Gizelle Bryant from “The Real Housewives of Potomac” and Lisa Barlow from “The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City.” Here’s what they say about what makes a housewife, well, one of the “Real Housewives.”
This interview was edited for clarity.
Luann: What makes a ‘Real Housewife’ today? A woman who can juggle it all — career, family, husbands —
Vicki:  — boyfriends, dating —
Luann: — travel, friendships. It’s a full-time occupation. It really is, and one that has changed the idea of what a housewife really is.
Gizelle: I think definitely a woman that can be comfortable in her own skin, knows who she is, confident, secure, and is OK to be vulnerable.
Lisa Barlow: Someone that’s completely authentic, that’s comfortable with themselves, that has a strong identity, and someone that’s bold.

Teresa: To me, a “Real Housewife” means being real, being true to yourself. Obviously we live in this world of, like, everything’s on the internet — being out there, you can’t let anyone bother you that’s writing things about you. You have to be really strong and just keep it moving.

Kyle: A “Real Housewife” on Bravo is somebody that can really juggle being a mom, being a wife, going through separation, having a career, being a good friend, being true to themselves, even if it’s not the popular thing to say or do at the time, and not be afraid of what other people think of you.

Vicki: A “Housewife” to me is authentic, not trying to create a storyline — they are the storyline. We see sometimes the new girls coming in and faking their reality — and I can’t stand that. Again, being a businesswoman — I think we all are, we can say that we are — being authentic. Going through the divorces on TV has been difficult for me. And then dating, difficult again. And so it’s a whole thing of real life. It’s not just being at home, cooking dinner and taking the kids to sports.
Luann: And for future “Housewives” out there — just be your authentic self.
Gizelle: Totally. Because we know when you’re not.
Vicki: And we might call you out on it.

title: Is Phil Collins A Swiftie? Music Icon Says Taylor Swift ‘Deserves’ To Be ‘Hugest Thing In The World’
summary: Phil Collins recently joined BBC Radio 2 program “Tracks of My Years with Vernon Kay” and gushed about Taylor Swift’s talent.
story: Phil Collins might actually be a Swiftie.
The legendary musician recently joined BBC Radio 2 program “Tracks of My Years with Vernon Kay” and gushed about Taylor Swift’s talent.

“I’m so pleased that she’s the hugest thing in the world now,” Collins said. “It kind of feels like she deserves it. It’s easy to knock someone that’s got so much success, but I think she really deserved it.”

During the program, Collins shared the 10 songs that have soundtracked his life, as is the premise of the show. One of the iconic singer’s chosen tunes was Swift’s “White Horse” off of her 2008 album “Fearless.”

Collins, 75, opened up about how he was introduced to the song when Swift performed it during the 2010 Songwriters Hall of Fame induction. The moment stuck with him, the iconic singer and drummer said.

“I’d kind of known the name, but she wasn’t anywhere near the star she is today. Very nice lady,” Collins recalled, adding that his daughter, actor Lilly Collins, had introduced him to Swift that day. “Then she got up on stage with the guitar, and sang “White Horse, and it blew me away completely.”
He praised both the song itself and its sentiment. But what really impressed Collins was Swift’s voice.
“She sang it beautifully, and it was just so simple, you know, her and the guitar,” he said on the program. “So I’ve always had a soft spot for this song since then.”
Collins other selections included “I Want To Hold Your Hand” by The Beatles and the Martha and the Vandellas’ “Dancing In The Street.”

The critically acclaimed singer, drummer and songwriter, known for his hits including “In the Air Tonight,” “Easy Lover” and “Another Day in Paradise,” knows music. Collins, whose career spans more than 50 years, was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame himself in 2003.
He’ll also soon be a two-time inductee into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Collins was already inducted in 2010 as part of his band Genesis. And in November, he’ll be inducted as a solo artist.

“A defining voice of his era, Collins has influenced generations of musicians, and his songs continue to resonate on radio, in film, and across streaming platforms,” the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame said on its website.

Swift, 36, has also been steadily cementing her own legacy in the halls of music history. In June 2026, she was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, making her the youngest female artist with the distinction.

title: ‘Doppelgängers’ Snoop Dogg, Backstreet Boys’ Kevin Richardson Finally Meet And It’s Glorious
summary: Rapper Snoop Dogg and Backstreet Boys’ band member Kevin Richardson have long been called “twins” by the internet. Recently, they met at the premiere of “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie”
story: With their lengthy locks, goatees and sharp jawlines, rapper Snoop Dogg and Backstreet Boys’ band member Kevin Richardson have long been called “twins” by the internet.
Heck, for a while there was a possibility they were the same person. I mean, no one’s ever seen them in the same room — until now.
While at the recent premiere of “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” in Los Angeles, the two parties finally met. And the moment was pretty darn glorious.
“It finally happened...iykyk” the boy band wrote in their Instagram post, shared on Aug. 5.
Fans, understandably, went wild.
“Why are there two Snoops in this picture?” one fan wrote in the comments.
Another fan wrote that they were “gonna sleep good tonight knowing this finally happened 🙌”
One social media user also pointed out that the two artists don’t just share their looks in common.
“Brothers, Calvin and Kevin lol. I’m just making that similar name connection,” the social media user said. “Also, they are both October Libras born in 1971 only 17 days apart. How fascinating!”

The two have been the subject of lookalike memes for years and the comparison stretches back even further — think decades.  Somehow, between all the appearances these guys have made at music events and more, they haven’t been able to unite until this moment.

“Paw Patrol” seems like an appropriate reason for the “twins” to come together, considering they’re both involved in the franchise. Snoop, who was born Calvin Broadus Jr., voices the character Dave in the upcoming movie, which is set to hit theaters on Aug. 14. Meanwhile Richardson’s Backstreet Boys dropped the song “Bottle Up” which is also featured in the animated comedy.
Hey, it’s nuthin but a twin thang.

title: People Can’t Handle How Closely This ‘Maverick’ Resembles Tom Cruise
summary: The San Francisco Giants hosted a “Top Gun” night Aug. 7 in celebration of the movie’s 40th anniversary this year. And the man who threw out the first pitch had fans questioning whether the film’s star Tom Cruise was actually on the mound.
story: The resemblance is truly uncanny.

The San Francisco Giants hosted a “Top Gun” night Aug. 7 in celebration of the movie’s 40th anniversary this year. And the man who threw out the first pitch had fans questioning whether the film’s star Tom Cruise was actually on the mound.

In a video of the ceremonial pitch, shared by the Giants’ home stadium Oracle Park, “Maverick” takes the mound, dressed in his iconic flight jacket and aviator shades.  He’s even got Cruise’s signature flashy smile and charisma as he throws the ball to a “Top Gun” fan behind the plate.

Fans weren’t sure what to make of the Maverick lookalike, with several social media users even asking whether the video was generated by AI. Others wondered if they were seeing a young Tom Cruise was on the mound.
“Spitting image,” one Instagram user said.

It turns out that the mystery man is a Maverick impersonator named Jerome LeBlanc, who goes by the “California Tom Cruise.” LeBlanc, who’s been working as the impersonator for about 17 years, makes hundreds of appearances a year.
He told NBC’s local Phoenix, Arizona affiliate 12 News that he started out performing as Maverick when he was 20 years old while pursuing an architecture degree at UCLA.
While LeBlanc has generated quite a bit of popularity as an impersonator, with more than 772,000 followers on TikTok, he’s also an artist who paints.
LeBlanc’s pitch must’ve been a lucky one, as the Giants ended up winning the game 5-2 against the Detroit Tigers.

title: Jason Sudeikis Cites the 1 ‘Ted Lasso’ Life Lesson That Made Him Come Back for Season 4
summary: Jason Sudeikis speaks about the fourth season of Ted Lasso and why he decided to make another season.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.
Jason Sudeikis has said Ted Lasso is just himself after two beers. So when I chat with the actor backstage at Studio 1A, I guess I’m speaking with the coach.

Sudeikis celebrated the premiere of “Ted Lasso” Season 4 on Aug. 5 with TODAY for not one, not two, but three live interviews, including with co-star Brendan Hunt and new cast members Tanya Reynolds, Faye Roberts, Jude Mack and Abbie Hern. The morning starts on the right foot when the 8:15 a.m. interview with Craig Melvin concludes with a stagehand carrying out two full pint glasses.

title: Watch Hoda Kotb’s Daughters Throw The Sweetest Surprise For Her 62nd Birthday
summary: Former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb shared an adorable video of a surprise that her daughters Haley Joy, 9, and Hope Catherine, 7, cooked up just ahead of her birthday on Aug. 9.
story: The sweetest thing about this birthday might not be actually be the cake.
Former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb shared an adorable video of a surprise that her daughters Haley Joy, 9, and Hope Catherine, 7, cooked up just ahead of her big day on Aug. 9.
The two girls managed to turn their home into the coolest birthday venue. And Kotb, who is turning 62 years old, was simply shocked.
“You guys, this is beautiful!” Kotb says in the video, posted on Instagram Aug. 7.

In the clip, Kotb walks down a hallway, through some rainbow streamers and into the living room where the area is decked out in shimmery, metallic balloons, family pictures and a big “Happy Birthday Mom” banner. Kotb’s dog Waffles appears to be equally stoked about the surprise.
King Harvest’s 1972 hit “Dancing in the Moonlight” plays in the background.
“This is my favorite song in the whole wide world,” an ecstatic Kotb says.
Hope quickly responds by telling her mom, ““I know! It was my idea!”
The celebration continued with some food as well, the video shows.

Kotb has had some pretty memorable birthdays, including several celebrations on the show.  The longtime journalist and television personality — who adopted her first daughter, Haley, in 2017, and second child, Hope, in 2019 — ended up making a major life decision amid her 60th birthday celebration. It was then that she felt it was time to begin thinking about a departure from the show.

“I realized that it was time for me to turn the page at 60, and to try something new,” an emotional Kotb said on TODAY in 2024. “I remembered standing outside looking at these beautiful bunch of people with these gorgeous signs, and I thought, ‘This is what the top of the wave feels like for me.’ And I thought it can’t get better, and I decided that this is the right time for me to kind of move on.”
Kotb, who currently hosts podcast “Making Space with Hoda Kotb” said she hoped to spend more time with her daughters.

Kotb, who left TODAY in January 2025 after 17 years on the show and 26 years at NBC News, has remained part of the NBC family. Her final formal day with the show ended with Kotb driving away in a minivan with her daughters.

title: Fleetwood Mac’s Lindsey Buckingham Says He and Steve Nicks ‘Talk All The Time’ After Years of Tension
summary: Guitarist Lindsey Buckingham told E! News at Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood event Aug. 6 that he and lead singer Stevie Nicks are on good terms.
story: It seems that Fleetwood Mac is sailing through some changing ocean tides.

Guitarist Lindsey Buckingham told E! News at Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood event Aug. 6 that he and lead singer Stevie Nicks, 78, chat it up regularly these days. The development comes after a famously tension-filled history between the two, who were not only bandmates but also exes. They feuded on and off for decades.
“Stevie and I are talking all the time now,” Buckingham, 76, told the outlet.

Buckingham attended the event to present the songwriter of the year award to artist Sombr. The guitarist, who joined Fleetwood Mac with Nicks on New Year’s Eve of 1974, said that the group has been working on a documentary, referring to the upcoming Apple TV project on the band. And it’s had an unexpected effect.

“That’s going to be coming out the very beginning of next year, so we are celebrating that,” Buckingham told E! News. “I think the process of making that has been a very circular healing process for all of us.”

The guitarist explained to the outlet that the band was in a rocky place in 2019. That year, the group had been on a roughly yearlong final concert tour, which spanned 80 shows across eight countries. However Buckingham was fired from the band in April 2018 before the tour even kicked off.

“We had left things in 2019, maybe as far as I was concerned, not in a very good place for all the wrong reasons,” he said of the band, whose lineup at the time included Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Nicks, and Christine McVie, along with new additions Mike Campbell and Neil Finn. Christine McVie died in 2022 at 79 years old.
“No one was happy about it, and all of that has been healed and worked out,” Buckingham said of the band’s issues following the tour.
However, Buckingham stopped short of implying that fans can expect any touring on the horizon.

Fleetwood Mac, one of the best-selling acts of all time, has been known for releasing hit after hit despite interband drama. Buckingham and Nicks joined the band while in a relationship, but cracks would soon develop. And during the recording of their legendary 1977 album “Rumours,” the two split. Additionally, John McVie and Christine McVie were navigating their own divorce. And Fleetwood’s marriage was falling apart as well.

The rocky breakup between Buckingham and Nicks led to classics on the album including “Dreams,” written by Nicks, and “Go Your Own Way,” by Buckingham. Though the pair initially stayed in the band, they both eventually departed between 1987 and 1991 to pursue their own projects.

The group came back together in the late 1990s for a tour. But following Buckinham’s firing, Nicks ceased all communication with her former flame until Christine McVie’s death prompted a brief reunion.

“The only time I’ve spoken to Lindsey was [at McVie’s memorial], for about three minutes,” Nicks told Rolling Stone in a 2024 interview. “I dealt with Lindsey for as long as I could. You could not say that I did not give him more than 300 million chances.”

However the two appeared to mend fences and last year, they reissued their 1973 album, “Buckingham Nicks,” on streaming and other formats. The project was made prior to their involvement in Fleetwood Mac.
Next year, which will mark the 50th anniversary of the iconic “Rumours” album, will be an “interesting” one, Buckingham told E! News.
“I think quite a few things will reveal themselves,” he said.

title: Here’s What Anthony Bourdain Shared About His Only Child Ariane
summary: Anthony Bourdain had one child, a daughter named Ariana Busia-Bourdain. Here is what he shared about her.
story: Anthony Bourdain left behind a lasting legacy when he died in 2018, but the world-renowned chef seemed to be most proud of his role as a father.
In April 2007, the author and television personality welcomed his first and only child, a daughter named Ariane Busia-Bourdain, with his second wife, Ottavia Busia.
Throughout his career, Bourdain spoke about his role as a father on multiple occasions, saying his daughter inspired him in many ways.

Nearly 10 years after his death by suicide, Bourdain’s career is in the spotlight once again with the release of “Tony,” a biopic that stars Dominic Sessa as a young Bourdain. The film is based on the opening chapters of the chef’s memoir, “Kitchen Confidential” and follows a 19-year-old Bourdain as he works at a restaurant in Cape Cod.

As fans of the late chef prepare to revisit the early days of his career with the new film, we’re taking a look back at Bourdain’s personal life and sharing everything he said about his most important job: father.
Becoming a Dad Influenced the Way Bourdain Thought About Life and Food
While speaking with The Associated Press in 2008, Bourdain reflected on the way his then-19-month-old daughter had changed his life.
“I feel obliged to at least do the best I can and not do anything really stupidly self-destructive if I can avoid it,” he said.
For instance, Bourdain quit smoking and said he began purchasing organic food for his daughter.
Bourdain Wanted His Daughter to Have a Diverse Palette
In that same AP interview, Bourdain said he wanted to encourage Ariane to try a wide array of foods from a young age.
“I very much don’t want her to fall into a groove where she wants a grilled cheese sandwich with the crusts cut off and nothing else,” he said.
When it came to food, the “Parts Unknown” star said he wanted to instill a sense of curiosity in his daughter.
“The sooner my child eats like an adult and the more often that she does, the happier I am,” he said.
Bourdain Said His Daughter Had Him ‘Wrapped Around Her Finger’
In 2013, Bourdain spoke with The Guardian and recalled how becoming a father at 50 years old influenced his life.

“I was finally old enough to be qualified for the job. Ariane has me wrapped around her finger. All I can realistically hope for is that she feels loved. That she has high self-esteem. And good martial-arts skills,” he said.
Bourdain Said His Daughter Shared His Passion for Cooking
During an interview with The Canadian Press in 2016, Bourdain said his daughter enjoyed making ratatouille after watching the Disney film by the same name.
“She gets to use a knife, which fills me with terror. It makes her very happy,” he said.
Bourdain made it a point to involve his daughter in the cooking process from a young age and said they regularly cooked together. One of their go-to dishes was breaded veal cutlets.

“The sooner they start, the better. I mean, in a perfect world, all teenagers would already know how to feed themselves and a few friends reasonably, competently, a few basics, just to be good citizens of the world. Sadly, that’s not the case,” he said.
The proud dad said his daughter loved it when he cooked meatballs, pasta and macaroni and cheese.
In 2021, Vanity Fair shared the following excerpt of the book “Bourdain: The Definitive Oral Biography,” which included his daughter’s own reflections on her relationship with her father.

“We’d cook schnitzel; he’d make little stations: one of them has the breading, one has the flour, one has the eggs, and my dad put it in the pan. He’d cook omelets for me all the time, and I’d help him flip it. He would let me sprinkle chocolate chips or blueberries into pancakes, and then he’d let me flip the pancake a little. When we were in the Hamptons, he’d cook dinner, cook breakfast, so that’s when he really cooked for me,” she said. “He taught me how to cut things and not chop off my fingers, to curl my fingers under. He gave me my own little knife, and I still have it, and still use it.”
Bourdain Paid Tribute to His Daughter in One of His Cookbooks
In his 2016 cookbook, “Appetites: A Cookbook,” Bourdain gave a nod to his daughter in the introduction.

“From the second I saw my daughter’s head corkscrewing out of the womb, I began making some major changes in my life,” he wrote. “I was no longer the star of my own movie — or any movie. From that point on, it was all about the girl. ... Fatherhood has been an enormous relief, as I am now genetically, instinctually compelled to care more about someone other than myself. I like being a father. No, I love being a father. Everything about it.”
Despite His Busy Work Schedule, Bourdain Prioritized Time With His Daughter
Bourdain spent a lot of time traveling for work, but he made sure to pencil in plenty of time with his daughter.
“I’ll go back, see my daughter, unpack, repack, mimic a normal life, which is extraordinarily pleasurable to me,” he told People in 2018.
Bourdain Raved About His Daughter in One of His Final Interviews
Just months before his death in 2018, Bourdain spoke with Popula and opened up about his parenting philosophy.
The chef told the publication that his girlfriend, Asia Argento, had some words of wisdom when she shared the following message with him: “Children create themselves independently of us.”
The words resonated deeply with Bourdain.

“All you can do is show,” he said. “Like, in my case, my daughter feels loved. She knows she’s loved. She has good self-esteem. Very important. And good martial arts skills. So no man, no boy ... she knows she can take any boy in her age group.”
Above all, Bourdain said he wanted her daughter to feel free to be her true self.

“That’s all I can do as a father,” he said. “I can’t pick all of the things that ... you know. I can’t. She’s so far ahead of me. I can’t pick her music, her boyfriends, whatever, however she’s going to turn out.”
Instead of helicopter parenting, Bourdain opted for a more streamlined approach and shared a few “basic things” with his daughter.
“I think how resolute she is, how much she wants to change the world, is willing to sacrifice in order to change the world,” Bourdain said. “That’s gonna have to come from within.”

title: Traffic Anchor Witnesses Car Crash When Reporting on Live TV and His Reaction Is Everything
summary: Traffic anchor KJ Jacobs had a candid and hilarious reaction while witnessing a car crash during a live report.
story: Live television is having a moment and one reporter’s latest reaction to an unexpected incident is going viral.
KJ Jacobs, meteorologist and traffic anchor for WCPO 9 in Cincinnati, Ohio, was delivering a live traffic report on Aug. 9, when he witnessed a car crash happen in real time.
While reporting how traffic was slowing down around a stalled car that was in the center lane on I-71, another car appeared to merge onto the highway and slammed into the stalled vehicle.

“Oh sh..!” Jacobs quickly reacted, before composing himself and adding, “Oh, I’m so sorry. This literally, just watched the crash happen in real time, and I almost said something inappropriate. But you can see this car just smash right into this car in real time.”
Jacobs professionally continued his report, describing the scene at hand from the live shot.
“So just watch this in real time, that impact right there. Can imagine what that felt like and what it would have sounded like had I heard it,” he continued.
Jacobs shared the video on his Instagram, captioning the clip, “A natural reaction on LIVE TV, but I’m so glad I hit the brakes just in time!”
People in the comments section applauded his reaction, with one person writing, “Then immediately reported the whole accident in detail.. A NATURAL JOURNALIST.”
“He didn’t close the ‘t’ on the word,” another commented about his blooper.
Telemundo and “Owning Manhattan” star Genesis Suero also wrote, “It happens to the best of us, especially those of us who do live TV.”
Others complained about people’s poor driving skills and noted that the footage will be good for the stalled car’s insurance company to review.
However, one person pointed out that live TV has recently been delivering headline worthy clips.

“Between him & homegirl on QVC, live TV has been having a moment,” they wrote, referring to Toni Brattin accidentally having a NSFW moment while promoting her “Hair Fabulous” line of wigs live on QVC.

Last month, KTLA News reporter Rachel Menitoff kept her cool while a cockroach landed on her during a live report. Then there was FOX13 Memphis anchor Dominique Dillon who fell asleep on the air, three months after returning from maternity leave.
In her Aug. 5 interview on TODAY, Dillion told Craig Melvin and Laura Jarrett she “was mortified,” but appreciated the public’s kind words and messages of support.
As for Jacobs, his traffic segment began getting more views. In the comments section, he shared that he was “stunned by the reaction.”

“Thank you to everyone who has watched, liked, commented, shared, and followed,” he wrote. “The encouragement from friends, family, longtime viewers, and so many new faces has been overwhelming in the best way.”
He added that he never imagined the oops moment would reach so many people across the country.
“I’m grateful you’re here, and I hope you’ll stick around for more weather, traffic, and a few laughs along the way,” he said. “Thank you!”

title: Meet the New Couple Falling in Love in ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2
summary: Crave announced that two new cast members are joining “Heated Rivalry” Season 2. Meet the two new stars.
story: “Heated Rivalry” Season 2 is expected to continue the love story between Shane and Ilya while introducing another couple to fall for: Harris and Troy.
Justice Smith will star as Harris Drover, and Charlie Gillespie will play Troy Barrett, joining the cast of Season 2, Canadian streamer Crave announced Aug. 7.

Smith most recently starred in 2025’s “Now You See Me: Now You Don’t” and saw public acclaim for his lead role in 2024’s “I Saw the TV Glow.” Gillespie is best known for his role as a lead singer of a teen boy band in Netflix’s “Julie and the Phantoms” and most recently featured in Will Gluck’s “One Night Only.”
In the casting announcement, Crave also confirmed that Season 2 of “Heated Rivalry” will air in spring 2027.

The casting of Troy and Harris also confirms long-running fan theories about where the “Heated Rivalry” story will go next. Season 1 was based on Rachel Reid’s “Game Changers” series, which consists of six — soon to be seven — novels.

Season 1 was based on Book 2 of the same name, “Heated Rivalry.” To continue the story of Shane and Ilya, played in the show by Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie, respectively, the sophomore outing is expected to follow the events of “The Long Game,” which is technically Book 6 in Reid’s series.

Two characters who feature prominently in “The Long Game” are Troy and Harris, who star in their own book, “Role Model” (the fifth “Game Changers” installment). In the book, Troy is a rough-and-tough hockey star who gets traded to one of the worst teams in the league (Ilya’s Ottawa Centaurs) and meets its peppy, out social media manager, Harris.
Filming for Season 2 is already underway. The official Instagram account for the show issued a statement Aug. 4 asking fans not to intrude on film sites.
“If you happen to come across one of our filming locations, please give our cast and crew the space they need to do what they do best,” they said.

As the onscreen story of “Heated Rivalry” continues, so, too, does the book series. Reid is currently at work on a seventh “Game Changers” novel — the third about Shane and Ilya —  called “Unrivaled,” set to follow the couple as they play on the same professional hockey team for the first time. “Unrivaled” is set for release in June 2027.
Less than a day before the latest casting news, Reid provided a writing update, posting a photo of a hefty stack of pages with the caption, “I hope you guys like Ilya and Shane…”

title: KATSEYE’s Sophia Laforteza Announces She’s Taking a Break From Group: ‘Health Has to Come First’
summary: Sophia Laforteza from KATSEYE announced that she is taking a break from the group to focus on her health.
story: Members of the popular girl group KATSEYE are lending support to their bandmate Sophia Laforteza as she prepares to take a break from the group to focus on her health.

The band issued a statement on Weverse, announcing that Laforteza will be “temporarily unable to participate in upcoming promotional activities” and noting that it’s “imperative that her mental health and wellness are prioritized.”

“Sophia has been receiving the utmost support, and following thorough consultations with medical professionals, it has been advised that she take dedicated time for extended rest and ongoing care to ensure a full recovery,” the statement read. “While Sophia herself is eager to perform alongside her members, the health, safety, and long-term well-being of our artists will always remain our highest priority.”
The statement continued, explaining that the band will “closely monitor (Sophia’s) progress and support her journey.”
“We plan to reassess her condition in September and will share a further update with fans at that time,” the statement read.
Laforteza addressed her fans directly in her own Instagram storypost.

“It truly breaks my heart to have to miss out on a lot. You know how much I love being on stage, performing, and sharing these moments with you,” she wrote. “Making this decision wasn’t easy, but I’m learning that health has to come first. I’m realizing that if I don’t take care of my mind and body now, I won’t be able to keep doing what I love the most for so long.”
The 23-year-old thanked her fans for being “patient” and “understanding.”
“It means more to me than I could ever say. I promise I’m going to work as hard as I can to get through this, heal properly, and come back stronger,” she wrote.
The singer ended her post by urging her fans to “be kind” and give KATSEYE “all your love and support.”
Laforteza did not attend the premiere of the “KATSEYE: Wild Hearts” documentary on Aug. 5. While addressing her bandmate’s absence, Lara Raj told Variety, “She’s not feeling well, but she says hi.”
Another member of KATSEYE, Manon Bannerman, revealed in February that she would be taking a temporary hiatus to “focus on her health and wellbeing,” per Variety.

“KATSEYE remains committed to showing up for one another and for the fans who mean everything to us. The group will continue scheduled activities during this time, and we look forward to being together again when the time is right,” the band’s statement read.
The group is scheduled to perform live on the TODAY Plaza on Aug. 14 as part of the Citi Concert Series.

title: Aaron Pierre Confirms He’s Single and Shares What He Really Thinks of Being the Internet’s Boyfriend
summary: Actor Aaron Pierre’s viral charm has earned him one of the coveted titles as “the internet’s boyfriend.” He reacts to the fame on TODAY.
story: Actor Aaron Pierre’s viral charm has earned him one of the coveted titles as “the internet’s boyfriend.” But on Aug. 7 on TODAY, he confirmed that as of now, he’s no one’s actual boyfriend.
“I’m just very locked into being the best father I can be and being the best artist I can be,” he told TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager and guest co-host Willie Geist.
“I’m just trying my best to get it right, and I never get it right. But I’m trying to get closer every day,” he added.

The relationship status reveal came after Jenna pointed out his heartthrob credentials, telling him that when his “Lanterns” co-star Kyle Chandler visited TODAY Aug. 3, he and Sheinelle joked about “getting lost” in Pierre’s eyes.
And Pierre isn’t exactly rushing to shut down “the internet’s boyfriend” hype.
“Listen, we’re all only human. I’d be lying to you if I said it wasn’t warmly received,” he said.

Although Pierre’s charms have fueled many viral moments online, his internet-boyfriend status really cemented after his appearance on “The Jennifer Hudson Show” in 2024, when his spirit tunnel video, featuring him dancing down a backstage corridor to the chant, “Aaron Pierre, that’s Mufasa,” amassed millions of views. Many fans re-created the viral video themselves, TODAY.com previously reported.
Pierre is next set to star in the DC Universe’s superhero series “Lanterns,” where he’ll play the role of John Stewart, a new recruit to the Green Lantern corps.
“John is such a beautifully dynamic and complex character, and it was such a joy, a privilege and an honor,” he told Jenna and Willie.
“Lanterns” is set to premiere Aug. 16.

title: Former Marine held in Russia for more than 4 years is back in the U.S.
summary: Former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman released from jail in Russia
story: A former U.S. Marine who spent more than four years in a Russian prison and is believed to be seriously ill was back in the United States Tuesday night, a White House official said.
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff said on X that he had the “profound privilege” of welcoming Robert Gilman, 32, home. He praised President Donald Trump for his release.
“He can now finally return to his family and receive the medical care he needs,” Witkoff said.
Trump earlier announced the release on Truth Social, saying Gilman was freed after he discussed the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Gilman, a teacher, was released “very much on a Humanitarian Basis,” with no exchange of prisoners having taken place. He was expected to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C.
The president added in his post that he had spoken to Gilman “and he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands. I will take care of that!”
The Russian government has not commented on the release.

About 50 days ago, Gilman was diagnosed with a “dissociative stupor — a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat,” Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., said in a statement following the man’s release.

“He was essentially catatonic and also suffered a severe case of pneumonia,” added Markey, who has been campaigning for Gilman’s release. “We don’t yet know the full details of his current condition or the long-term impact on his recovery.”
Gilman’s sister Lexie Hudson thanked Trump in a statement issued by Global Reach, an advocacy group representing his family.
“There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action,” she said.
“I am looking forward to seeing Robert. I haven’t been able to speak with him once since this all began,” she added. “We will make sure that he gets the treatment and support that he needs.”
Russia releases former Marine after four years in prison

Before his release, Hudson said in a statement Sunday that she was worried that he would die if he wasn’t freed. “I’m more afraid for my brother than I have been since this horrible nightmare started,” she said in the statement issued by Global Reach.

Her comments Sunday came around a month after Russia’s Kommersant newspaper reported that Gilman had been ​admitted to a hospital. Quoting his lawyer Irina Brazhnikova, the business daily reported that he was receiving treatment but it was too early to talk about a diagnosis.

Gilman, who served in the Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, had been detained in 2022. He was initially handed a 3 ½-year sentence for beating a police officer after being taken off a train for causing a disturbance.

While serving his sentence, Gilman was accused in October 2024 of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, beating an investigator and assaulting a guard; he was sentenced to eight years and one month.
Last year, his sentence was extended again to 10 years after he was found guilty of assaulting prison guards.
Gilman’s American supporters contend he was ill when he was first arrested and also that he was provoked while in prison into actions that led to further charges.
According to Markey, Gilman was “subjected to physical torture, forced medication, and provocations by Russian authorities” throughout his detention.
“There is no doubt that his treatment by Russian authorities is the reason Robert is in this precarious state today,” he added.
Gilman was one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia.

title: More than 160 people killed in Colombia’s strongest earthquake in years
summary: At least 132 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.
story: At least 169 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.

The worst-hit cities include Pereira, Cali, Quibdó, Manizales and Armenia, all of which remain under “red alert,” the nation’s highest-level disaster threat level, according to Colombia’s nonprofit Association of Capital Cities, which provided the death toll.
Seven airports have suspended operations, and hospitals, roads, transportation, aqueducts, energy and telecommunications have been disrupted in the areas hardest hit, it said.
Colombia’s newly inaugurated president, Abelardo De La Espriella, said in a national briefing that 700 people were injured in the temblor and an estimated 5,000 homes were damaged or destroyed.

title: ‘A piece of our history’: Untouched Roman shipwreck discovered off Italy
summary: Divers have uncovered a Roman-era shipwreck that had remained untouched on the seabed off Sicily for more than 2,000 years, police on the Mediterranean island said.
story: Divers have uncovered a Roman-era shipwreck that had remained untouched on the seabed off Sicily for more than 2,000 years, police on the Mediterranean island said.

Italian Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli described it on social media as “one of the most significant underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years,” with experts dating the vessel back to the first or second century B.C.

“The sea continues to reveal precious evidence of our history,” Giuli said. “This shipwreck tells the story of the people, trade routes, and exchanges that made the Mediterranean a crossroads of civilizations.”
After a tipoff from residents, the ship was discovered by divers  around 3 miles off Sicily’s western coast and about 150 feet below the surface, Italian authorities said in a statement.

title: Iran sets steep demands to reopen Hormuz despite hopes Oman deal could break impasse
summary: Tehran has vowed not to reopen the shipping lane “until America corrects its behavior,” despite a looming agreement with Oman.
story: There are no ongoing negotiations between Tehran and Washington, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday, after Tehran set out a steep series of demands for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
“The intermediaries are still making efforts to find ways to resume negotiations,” Araghchi said.

He tempered optimism stirred by Iran’s separate discussions with Oman over the future management of the waterway, saying that “changes to maritime routes in the Strait of Hormuz are a technical and legal matter and do not mean that the Strait of Hormuz has been reopened.”

Araghchi’s statement came a day after top Iranian security official Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr laid out the country’s conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, saying it would not do so “until America corrects its behavior.”

The statement from Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, as carried by Iranian state media, stated that the U.S. must withdraw its naval blockade, pay Iran damages for the war, unfreeze Iranian assets, lift sanctions on Tehran and permanently end the conflict against Iran and its regional allies.
Even though the demands are steep, analysts say they are still largely within the framework of the initial deal the two sides reached in June.

“The Supreme National Security Council of Iran, which is really a consensus body, they have come to a realization that for them the best route is returning back to the MOU,” Mehran Haghirian, director of research and programs at the Bourse & Bazaar Foundation London-based think tank, said in a phone interview.
“They want to make sure that they get some of those things up-front, or at least there is a process for them before there is any movement on Hormuz.”
The U.S. has yet to respond publicly to the list of conditions. Top officials have previously ruled out making any immediate payments to Iran during past efforts to seal a deal to end the war.

The country’s enriched uranium stockpile has also been a sticking point for Washington, which insists Iran must abandon its nuclear ambitions. The stalled negotiations have left the Strait of Hormuz largely impassable for months, save for brief periods of operation. Thousands of sailors remain stranded in the region, unable to return home or keep the world’s supply of oil flowing.

“What we’re really working through now is how you can actually set up a traffic scheme so that the ships that pass can pass through safely,” Vice President JD Vance told Fox News on Saturday. That scheme, Vance said, would include demining efforts and also assurances from Tehran that it would not fire on transiting vessels.

On Saturday, Oman condemned attacks on the vessels that were attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, saying in a statement that such attacks could affect its negotiations with Iran over the waterway’s management. The UAE and Kuwait on Saturday also condemned an Iranian missile attack on an Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. tanker.
Oman nonetheless said its discussions with Iran were “proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere.”

Iran and Oman, neighbors across the Strait of Hormuz, have been negotiating an agreement on how to manage traffic through the waterway, including considerations of a toll fee. The discussions have also been viewed optimistically, raising hopes that they could finally lead to reopening the strait.
But Iranian officials have dismissed any such possibility. Iran’s discussions with Oman do “not mean the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” Araghchi said Saturday.

Even though the Iranian officials say the discussions don’t mean an immediate reopening of Hormuz, Haghirian said the discussions would lay critical groundwork for if and when Iran reaches an agreement with the U.S. over Hormuz.

Iranian state media on Sunday reported that President Masoud Pezeshkian had met with the country’s absent Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, discussing “the war and the future ahead.” No evidence was provided that the meeting took place.

Pezeshkian earlier this week said that it had been “very difficult” to contact the 56-year-old leader, who has not been seen publicly since he was badly injured in the U.S. strikes that killed his father.
Meanwhile, the Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen again attacked Saudi Arabia on Sunday, with Yemen’s news agency saying the forces targeted the Mocha port along the Red Sea.

The Houthis have launched several attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent days, also hitting a Saudi Aramco oil refinery in the port city of Jizan with a drone. It said Sunday that the attack on the refinery was in response to Saudi drones’ incursions into the Saada and Hajjah airspaces of Yemen.
The Saudi Energy Ministry said Sunday on X that the fire that broke out at the refinery had been extinguished and nobody was injured.

The world’s top oil exporter, Aramco, is seeking to reroute some of its exports to the Red Sea instead of the Persian Gulf in an effort to circumvent the shuttered Strait of Hormuz. Riyadh on Saturday condemned the attacks by the Houthis, who it said had attacked the kingdom since July 13 and shipping vessels since July 22.

title: Israel rejects Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ⁠said Israeli forces wouldn’t withdraw from the war-torn enclave until Hamas fully disarms
story: Israel will not accept the 15-point plan for Gaza set out by President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday.

“I want to clarify this: Israel rejects the 15-point document. I have heard people saying, ‘You didn’t say that.’ So here I am saying it again,” he told a Cabinet meeting, referring to the peace plan set out by Trump last year. “The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed,” he added.
Trump last month touted a breakthrough in his Gaza peace plan, saying that Hamas has agreed to lay down arms.

The peace plan called for a phased withdrawal of Israel’s troops from Gaza alongside the disarmament of Hamas, but Netanyahu said Israeli forces are not going anywhere until Hamas completely disarms first.
“When I say Hamas must be disarmed, I mean heavy weapons, lighter weapons, all weapons. We are talking about genuine disarmament, not a fictitious one,” Netanyahu said Sunday.

Hamas had last month said that it would disarm, but only after Israel withdraws completely and stops all hostilities. The group also said that laying down its heavy weapons would come later in the process, conditional on the establishment of a Palestinian state.

Netanyahu, meanwhile, reaffirmed that “as long as I am prime minister, there will be no Palestinian state.” The leader is currently facing a domestic political battle for survival ahead of elections set for October, with the status of the Gaza and Iran wars likely to prove pivotal.

The explicit rejection of the peace plan, frequently touted by Trump as a key foreign policy achievement, also comes after months of growing tensions between the White House and Israel’s leadership over Iran. The White House did not immediately comment on the remarks.

Netanyahu said of Washington: “We are currently discussing this issue with the Americans. They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand firm on these matters.”

The Israeli leader may consider it worthwhile to “enter a new confrontation with President Trump,” said Ronni Shaked, a research fellow at the Harry S. Truman Institute at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, as his own popularity wanes ahead of October’s election.

“After three years, he is without any victory, and he just wants to show now to the people of Israel, before the election, that look at me, I have victory, and the victory is that we are going to disarm Hamas,” Shaked said in a phone interview, referring to the tactic as an “illusion.”

Responding to Netanyahu’s statement Sunday, senior Hamas official Basim Naeem said that the group expects the mediators and the U.S. to “exert pressure” on Netanyahu and his government to abide by the road map and “prevent him from obstructing the process for domestic political and electoral considerations.”

A further Hamas statement reaffirmed its commitment to the agreed-upon road map, reiterating the group’s “seriousness in engaging responsibly in implementing the fifteen points agreed upon and establishing a clear timetable for their implementation.”

Mohammad Dahlan, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, said Netanyahu’s announcement “represents a challenge, contempt, and deception of the American administration and President Trump’s team,” adding that Washington “now realizes that Netanyahu is an obstacle to achieving security and stability.”

Netanyahu’s far-right finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, welcomed his announcement after seeking to pressure the leader into a more hard-line stance. “I congratulate the Prime Minister for responding to our demand and clarifying unequivocally,” he said on X.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, meanwhile, “emphasized the necessity for all parties to fulfill their commitments and refrain from taking any actions that could hinder the implementation process or undermine the progress achieved,” his office said in a statement.

Despite agreeing to halt attacks in October, Israel has continued its deadly strikes on the Palestinian enclave. On Saturday, recovery operations concluded at the Karam Building in Gaza after 19 bodies were found under the rubble, according to the Gaza civil defense. Israel and Hamas both regularly accuse the other of breaching the ceasefire.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Oct. 7, 2023, according to the enclave’s health officials, including more than 1,200 people since the ceasefire began in October. Israel launched its war in Gaza in response to the Hamas-led attack in which around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.

title: Student kills multiple people at Thai school after fatally shooting grandparents
summary: At least one teacher was killed and four other people injured by a student who opened fire at a school in Thailand on Friday before killing himself, authorities said.
story: BANGKOK — A gunman shot and killed his grandparents before killing five people and himself at a school outside Bangkok on Friday, Thailand’s prime minister said, in the Southeast Asian nation’s worst mass killing since 2022.

Anutin Charnvirakul told a news conference that five teachers were shot dead and at least 30 people were injured in the shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in the Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province, north of Bangkok. The shooter took his own life, he added.

The perpetrator was identified as a student and police said that he had fired at least 26 rounds and that 34 other rounds of ammunition were found at the scene. They said they had recovered a 9 mm handgun believed to belong to his grandfather.
At least two people were in critical condition, police said.
One 18-year-old student told Reuters that at first he thought he was hearing firecrackers.
“Then it started getting more frequent, like ‘bang, bang, bang’ and then it went quiet at one point,” he said. “And the shooting started again.”
In a statement, the school said the shooting had “shaken the hearts” of students, parents, teachers and others.
The government said Anutin had directed relevant agencies to provide immediate and comprehensive support to all those affected.

“We rushed to care for the injured and I have dispatched the relevant personnel to handle the situation at the site,” Anutin told reporters. “This is very terrible, it is something that should not have happened.”
It is the second school shooting in Thailand this year.
One teacher was killed and a student was injured in February at a school in the southern district of Hat Yai.
In recent years, there has been a series of deadly shootings at schools and other locations in Thailand, where gun ownership is common.
Last year, six people were killed when a man opened fire at a Bangkok market before taking his own life.
In 2023, a 14-year-old killed two people and injured five others in a shooting at a luxury mall in Bangkok.

The previous year, a former police officer killed 36 people during a three-hour shooting and stabbing spree in the country’s northeast. Among his victims were 22 children he stabbed at a day care center.
A Thai soldier also killed 29 people in a shooting rampage in the northeastern city of Nakhon Ratchasima in 2020.

After the 2023 mall shooting, Anutin, who was interior minister at the time, enacted a one-year ban on the issue of new personal gun licenses and suspended public carry permits, among other gun control measures. The suspension of public carry permits was extended earlier this year.
“This is the reason why the government doesn’t allow arm carrying and extension of gun licenses,” Anutin said Friday. “This is the reason why.”

Anutin also vowed to introduce a new firearms control law in Southeast Asia’s largest gun-owning nation, according to Reuters. “The new law will only allow government officials on duty to carry guns,” the agency reported him saying.

As of 2017, Thai civilians were estimated to possess about 10.3 million firearms, or about 15 per 100 residents, according to the Small Arms Survey, a Swiss group that favors gun control. That compared with more than 393 million firearms in civilian possession in the United States, or 120.5 per 100 residents.
Nat Sumon reported from Bangkok, and Jennifer Jett from Hong Kong.
